<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/viewing-audit-logs","lastmod":"2026-05-23T07:06Z","nid":"1539933"} -->
## Viewing Audit Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-audit-logs
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Getting Started > Admin Portal > Viewing Audit Logs
- Last modified: 2026-05-23T07:06Z
- Summary: How to view and export audit logs in the Zscaler Security Operations platform.

Audit logs track user-initiated actions within the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform. This enables you to monitor configuration changes, such as updates to reports, data source instances, and outegrations. You can download specific audit logs for immediate review, and schedule automated exports to an external destination such as an Amazon S3 bucket.

Audit logs track key events including:

- Configuration of grouping rules and rule sets.
- Configuration of severity, score, and SLA settings.
- Creating, managing, and assigning roles and content permissions.
- Configuring field unification rule set.
- Configuring UI configurations.
- Updates to account settings and user settings.
- Management of data source mapping, data source instances, and data source scheduling.
- Configuration and mapping of outegrations.
- Changes to dashboards and reports.

## Viewing the Audit Logs Page

To view the Audit Logs page:

1. Go to a configuration page to: The configuration page for a user is provided here as an example. See image.
  - For a user: Click the profile menu in the top navigation bar, then click **Profile Settings**.
  - For an account: Click the profile menu in the top navigation bar, then click **Account Settings**.
  - For a source: Go to **Configure** > **Sources**, then click a source.
  - For an outegration: Go to **Configure**> **Outegrations**, then click an outegration.
  - For a report: Go to an app (**Vulnerabilities**, **Assets**, etc.), click **My Reports**, and click a report.
2. Click the **More**menu, and click **Audit Logs**. The **Audit Logs** page appears.
3. On the **Audit Logs** page for a user, you can do the following: See image.
  - Filter and sort the logs by operation, type, and user name.
  - Download the logs as a CSV file.
  - View additional information by clicking the arrow icon. See image.

Audit logs are retained for 90 days. To extend the retention period and to maintain a long-term history, you can export the logs to an Amazon S3 bucket or any other configured log destination.

[Image: Configuration Page of a User]

## Configuring Audit Log Export

You can schedule audit logs to be sent on a daily or hourly basis via an S3 outegration.

To configure automated audit log export for a user:

1. Click the profile menu in the top navigation bar, then click **Account Settings**. The **Settings**page appears.
2. Click the **Audit Logs Export** drop-down menu. See image.
3. Select **Enable Scheduling**, then select the following options: See image.
  1. **Included Entities**: Select the entity types to be included in the audit log (e.g., **Severity Score Settings**, **UI Configuration**).
  2. **Frequency**: Define the time interval for the audit log export (e.g., **Daily**or **Hourly**).
  3. **Select S3 Outegration**: Select **AWS S3**. To create an AWS S3 outegration, see [Creating Outegrations](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-outegrations).
4. Click **Save**. Audit logs are automatically exported to the designated AWS S3 bucket based on the defined scheduling frequency.

[Image: Audit Logs Page]

[Image: Additional Details]

[Image: Account Settings Page]

[Image: Audit Logs Export Drop-Down Menu]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/viewing-managing-assets-aem","lastmod":"2026-04-12T07:06Z","nid":"1538663"} -->
## Viewing & Managing Assets in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-managing-assets-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Remediate for AEM > Viewing & Managing Assets in AEM
- Last modified: 2026-04-12T07:06Z
- Summary: How to view and manage asset details in the Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) application in the SecOps platform.

An asset in the Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) app represents a single asset in your environment, unified (i.e., merged) and enriched with information from multiple sources. Selecting an asset on the Assets page opens its drawer, where you can view detailed information and perform multiple actions for the asset. To learn more, see About Assets in AEM.

The actions you can perform in the asset drawer depend on your user role in the AEM app. To learn more, see [Understanding System Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/understanding-system-roles) and [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/creating-custom-roles).

The asset drawer can be configured by admins and might look different in your account. The information provided in this article refers to the default asset drawer settings.

To view the asset drawer:

1. In the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar. See image.
2. Click the asset you want to view. See image. A drawer appears with the following details and tabs:
  - Top Panel
  - Details
  - Asset Merging
  - Findings
  - Tickets
3. Click **Apply Changes** after making changes to the asset, or close the drawer.

In the top panel of the asset drawer, you can view:

- **Name**: The name of the asset.
- **First Seen**: The asset's first seen date.

Additionally, you can perform the following actions:

- Copy a shareable link to the asset you're viewing.
- View the asset ID.
- Expand the asset's drawer to full screen.
- Close the asset drawer.
- View the asset's severity level and severity score. By default, it reflects the highest severity score among the findings detected on the asset.

On the **Details**tab, you can view:

- **Asset Type**: The classification or category that the asset belongs to, such as server, workstation, or application.
- **Sources**: The sources that the findings on the asset were detected.
- **Assignee**: The agent or team responsible for handling the asset.
- **Risk Mass**: The asset's cumulative risk exposure, calculated by summing the severity scores of active findings for each severity level (i.e., Critical, High, Medium, Low), and rounding the result. This indicator can be used to prioritize assets with similar risk profiles.
- **Has PII Data**: Indicates whether the asset contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII), highlighting its sensitivity and compliance requirements.

On the **Asset Merging**tab, you can view the original source records that the asset was merged from.

Additionally, you can perform the following actions:

- Apply filters to adjust the displayed assets by relevant attributes (e.g., filtering the original source records owner ID or first seen date).
- Adjust the displayed columns and their sorting settings. To learn more, see [Managing Table Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-table-columns).
- Click the **Export as CSV**icon to export the list of assets that the current asset was merged from as a CSV file.

On the **Findings**tab, you can explore the findings that were detected on the asset.

To view the finding's details (e.g., descriptions and score calculation logic), you can either expand the finding or drill down to the finding drawer.

Additionally, you can perform the following actions:

- Apply filters to adjust the displayed findings by relevant attributes and to explore the asset's risk portfolio (e.g., filtering the findings by a particular state, title, or severity score).
- To update key finding details, select the findings and click **Update**. The fields available to update include fields that were enabled for manual override in Configure > Data Model.
- Click the**Export as CSV**icon to export findings on the asset to a CSV file.
- Adjust the displayed columns and their sorting settings. To learn more, see [Managing Table Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-table-columns).

On the **Tickets**tab, you can view all tickets related to the asset and a summary of their details, sources, status, and remediation percentage.

Additionally, you can perform the following actions:

- Apply filters to adjust the displayed tickets by relevant attributes (e.g., filtering the tickets by type, title, or severity score).
- Adjust the displayed columns and their sorting settings. To learn more, see [Managing Table Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-table-columns).

Clicking a ticket opens its drawer. To return to the asset drawer, click the asset name in the top-left corner of the ticket drawer.

## Viewing the OS End of Life Dashboard

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-os-end-life-dashboard
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Analyze for AEM > Viewing the OS End of Life Dashboard
- Last modified: 2026-08-07T05:17Z
- Summary: How to view the OS End of Life dashboard in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform.

The OS End of Life dashboard provides visibility into assets running operating systems that have reached or are approaching End-of-Life (EOL) or End-of-Support (EOS) status. The dashboard includes summary tiles, charts, and tables that provides details of the EOL and EOS status of OS assets.

Identifying high-risk assets helps organizations:

- Mitigate security risks in unpatched and unsupported operating systems.
- Strengthen regulatory and internal compliance posture.
- Minimize operational disruptions due to outdated OS versions.

To create an OS EOL dashboard from a preconfigured template, go to Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > OS End of Life. To learn more, see [Using Dashboard Templates](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-dashboard-templates).

## Top Assets

The tiles display the total number of assets, including those that are reaching the EOL or EOS date, and the ones that have already reached the EOL or EOS date.

[Image: High-level overview of assets in EOL or EOS]

- Total Active Assets in EOL
- Assets Reaching EOL in the Next 6 Months
- Total Active Assets in EOS
- Assets Reaching EOS in the Next 6 Months

The number of active OS assets past their EOL date, which no longer receive security patches or updates. It directly measures the organization's security risk by revealing the total count of vulnerable OS assets. Click the asset number to view the list of active OS assets in EOL.

See image.

The number of OS assets reaching EOL in the next 6 months. This helps in proactive budgeting, migration, or replacement before an asset becomes a security liability. Click the asset number to view the list of OS assets.

The number of active OS assets past their EOS date. This data helps with effective security and risk management. Click the asset number to view the list of OS assets at EOS.

The number of OS assets reaching EOS in the next 6 months. The 6-month window provides necessary visibility for long-term planning, budgeting, or scheduling maintenance cycles well in advance. Click the asset number to view list of OS assets approaching EOS status in the next 6 months.

[Image: List of total active assets in EOL]

## Widgets

The charts and tables provide a detailed breakdown of key metrics categorized by EOL and EOS status.

- Assets in EOL Overtime
- Assets in EOS Overtime
- OS EOL - Breakdown by Asset OS - Top 10
- OS EOS - Breakdown by Asset OS - Top 10
- OS EOL - Breakdown by Asset Owner - Top 5
- OS EOS - Breakdown by Asset Owner - Top 5
- OS EOL - Breakdown by Asset Type
- OS EOS - Breakdown by Asset Type

The chart shows the historical trend of OS assets that are no longer supported by their vendors. This is critical for tracking the organization's performance in managing and reducing high-risk EOL assets. A consistent downward trend indicates successful remediation efforts. Conversely, a stable or upward trend signals that remediation is not keeping pace with assets reaching EOL, allowing you to identify and address issues. The chart's default view displays data from the last three months.

See image.

Click a date on the timeline, and click **View Items** to see a detailed list of active OS assets at EOL for that date.

See image.

The chart shows the historical trend of active OS assets in EOS. It helps track the growth of unsupported assets to prioritize upgrades. A rising trend indicates growing technical debt and security exposure, as these assets are not receiving essential security updates. Monitoring this trend is crucial for maintaining a secure and reliable IT environment. The chart's default view displays data from the last three months.

See image.

Click a date on the timeline, and click **View Items** to see a detailed list of active OS assets at EOS for that date.

See image.

This chart lists the top 10 operating systems with the highest number of assets affected by EOL. It helps track OS assets using two metrics:

- **Active Assets in EOL**: The dark blue bar represents assets currently in EOL, highlighting security risks and compliance gaps that require urgent attention.
- **Active Assets with OS EOL in 6 Months**: The light blue bar represents assets approaching EOL in the next 6 months.

See image.

To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select **Click to View Items**to view details of the individual assets for the selected OS.

See image.

This chart lists the top 10 operating systems with the highest number of assets affected by EOS. It helps track OS assets using two metrics:

- **Active Assets in EOS**: The dark blue bar represents the current count of assets running on an OS unsupported by its vendor. This indicates a high risk as these assets no longer receive security patches or technical support.
- **Active Assets with OS EOS in 6 Months**: The light blue bar represents the number of assets running operating systems whose support period is scheduled to expire within the next 6 months. This acts as an early warning signal, allowing you to identify potential vulnerabilities before they become active threats.

See image.

To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select **Click to View** to see the details of the individual assets for the selected OS.

See image.

This chart shows the top 5 owners (e.g., EUC team, Enterprise API team) of assets that are currently at EOL and nearing their EOL date within the next 6 months. It helps track asset ownership using two metrics:

- **Total Active Assets with OS EOL Upcoming in the Next 6 Months**: The dark blue bars represent active assets that will become unsupported within the next 6 months.
- **Active Assets in EOL**: The light blue bars represent active assets already past their EOL date.

See image.

To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select **Click to View Items**to view details of the individual assets for the selected asset owner.

See image.

This chart shows the top 5 owners of assets that are currently unsupported and nearing their EOS date within the next 6 months (e.g., EUC team, Enterprise API team). It helps track asset ownership using two metrics:

- **Active Assets in EOS**: The dark blue bars represent active assets already past their EOS date.
- **Total Active Assets with OS EOS Upcoming in the Next 6 Months**: The light blue bars represent active assets that will become unsupported within the next 6 months.

This ensures that ownership of remediation is clearly defined and actionable.

See image.

To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select **Click to View Items** to view details of the individual assets for the selected asset owner.

See image.

View OS assets that are currently at EOL and nearing their EOL date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g., Windows workstation, Linux). This enables targeted risk prioritization, allows for tailored remediation strategies, and facilitates accurate budget allocation.

See image.

To investigate further, click the corresponding asset number in the Active Assets in EOL column to see details of individual assets for the selected asset type.

See image.

View OS assets that are currently unsupported and nearing their EOS date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g., Windows workstation, Linux). This helps teams prioritize immediate security risks, refine IT migration plans, allocate budget, and simplify compliance requirements.

See image.

To investigate further, click the corresponding asset number in the Active Assets in EOS column to see details of individual assets for the selected asset type.

See image.

## Viewing Policy Violations in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-policy-violations-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Remediate for AEM > Viewing Policy Violations in AEM
- Last modified: 2025-11-11T13:58Z
- Summary: Information about the policy violation drawer details and actions in the Asset Exposure Management (AEM) application in the SecOps platform.

Policy violations represent deviations from established security policies detected on assets within the Asset Exposure Management (AEM) app in the Zscaler SecOps platform. Clicking a policy violation on the Policy Violations page opens the violation's drawer, where you can view detailed information including the affected asset, policy name, and severity score. You can also perform multiple actions for the violation. To learn more, see [About Policy Violations](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/about-policy-violations-operational-view-aem).

The actions you can perform in the violation drawer depend on your user role in the AEM app. To learn more, see [Understanding System Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/understanding-system-roles) and [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-custom-roles).

To view the policy violation drawer:

1. Go to the AEM app.
2. In the left-side navigation, click **Policy Violations**. See image.
3. Click the policy violation you want to view. See image. A drawer appears with the following details:
  - Top Panel
  - Details
  - Asset Info
4. Close the drawer to return to the **Policy Violations** page.

[Image: policy violations table in AEM]

[Image: policy violation drawer]

In the top panel of the policy violation drawer, you can view:

- **Title:** The policy violation's title, as assigned by the source.
- **First Seen:** The date the policy violation was first detected.
- **Severity Score:** The original severity score and the contextualized score for the policy violation.
- **ID:** The unique identifier of the policy violation.
- **State:** The current state of the policy violation (e.g., **Active**or **Inactive**).

Additionally, you can perform the following actions:

- Copy a shareable link to the violation.
- Expand the violation drawer to full screen.
- Close the violation drawer.

On the **Details**tab, you can view:

- **Asset Name:** The name of the asset affected by the policy violation.
- **Type:** The type of asset impacted (e.g., **Workstation**, **Web Application**).
- **Sources:** The source that reported the policy violation.
- **First Seen:** The date the policy violation was initially detected.
- **Last Seen:** The most recent date the policy violation was detected.
- **Policy Name:** The name of the policy that was violated (e.g., **EDR Coverage**).
- **Policy Violation Type:** The category of the policy violation (e.g., **Tool Coverage**).
- **Assignee:** The user or team assigned to remediate this policy violation.
- **SLA:** The service level agreement (SLA) date that the policy violation must be remediated by.

On the **Asset Info**tab, you can view:

- **Asset IP**: The IP address assigned to the asset (e.g., **74.69.111.39**).
- **Asset Type**: The category or classification of the asset (e.g., **Web Application**).
- **Asset Name**: The name of the asset (e.g., **https://acmeprod.com**).
- **Asset Owner**: The team or individual responsible for managing the asset (e.g., **Networking Team**).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Viewing Violation Tickets in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-violation-tickets-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Remediate for AEM > Viewing Violation Tickets in AEM
- Last modified: 2026-02-17T06:06Z
- Summary: Information about the violation ticket drawer details and actions in the Asset Exposure Management (AEM) application in the SecOps platform.

Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) violation tickets aggregate related policy violations into a single work item that can be fixed as one task. Selecting a violation ticket from the Violation Tickets page opens the violation ticket's drawer, where you can view detailed information and perform multiple actions for the violation ticket. To learn more, see [About Violation Tickets](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/about-violation-tickets-operational-view-aem).

The actions you can perform in the violation ticket drawer depend on your user role in AEM. To learn more, see [Understanding System Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/understanding-system-roles) and [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-custom-roles).

To view the violation ticket drawer:

1. Go to the AEM app.
2. In the left-side navigation, click **Violation Tickets**. See image.
3. Click the violation ticket you want to view. See image. A drawer appears with the following details:
  - Top Panel
  - Details
  - Policy Violations
  - Assets
4. Click **Apply Changes** after making updates to the violation ticket.

[Image: Violation Tickets table in UVM]

[Image: violation ticket drawer]

In the top panel of the violation ticket drawer, you can view:

- **Title:** The violation ticket's title set by your account's grouping rules.
- **First Seen:** The earliest detected policy violation included in the violation ticket.
- **Severity Score:** The violation ticket's severity score.
- **Status:** The current workflow status of the violation ticket (e.g., **New**, **Open**, **In Progress**, or **Closed**).

Additionally, you can perform the following actions:

- Copy a shareable link to the violation ticket.
- View the violation ticket's ID.
- Expand the violation ticket drawer to full screen.
- Close the violation ticket drawer.

On the **Details**tab, you can view:

- **SLA:** The service-level agreement (SLA) date that the violation ticket must be remediated by.
- **Assignee:** The user or team assigned to handle the violation ticket.
- **Policy Violations Count:** The total number of policy violations aggregated into the violation ticket.
- **Update CMDB**: Update asset records in your CMDB. This drop-down menu only appears if assets with incomplete, inaccurate, or inconsistent data are detected within your CMDB (ServiceNow CMDB).
- **Grouping Details**: Specifies the grouping rule and the rule set that grouped the findings into the violation ticket. This is useful when investigating whether your account's grouping logic needs to be adjusted. To learn more, see Configuring Grouping Rules.

On the **Policy Violations**tab, you can view all the policy violations aggregated into the violation ticket. You can:

- Apply filters to adjust the displayed policy violations by relevant attributes (e.g., **Severity**, **Policy Name**).
- Drill down into individual policy violations to view additional details in the policy violation drawer.
- Click the **Export as CSV**icon to export policy violations in the violation ticket to a CSV file.
- Adjust the displayed columns and their sorting settings. To learn more, see [Managing Table Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-table-columns).

On the **Assets**tab, you can view the list of assets affected by the policy violations contained in the violation ticket. You can perform the following actions:

- Apply filters to adjust the displayed assets by relevant attributes (e.g., **Asset Type**, **Last Seen**).
- Drill down into individual assets to view additional details in the asset drawer.
- Select an asset and click **Update**to update the asset's details. The fields available to update include fields that have been enabled for manual override in Configure > Data Model.
- Click the **Export as CSV**icon to export assets in the violation ticket to a CSV file.
- Adjust the displayed columns and their sorting settings. To learn more, see [Managing Table Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-table-columns).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/viewing-violation-tickets-dashboard","lastmod":"2026-08-07T05:17Z","nid":"1540176"} -->
## Viewing the Violation Tickets Dashboard

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-violation-tickets-dashboard
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Analyze for AEM > Viewing the Violation Tickets Dashboard
- Last modified: 2026-08-07T05:17Z
- Summary: How to view the Violation Tickets Dashboard in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform.

The Violation Tickets Dashboard in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform offers visibility into your team's progress in identifying, managing, and resolving violation tickets. This dashboard enables you to view open violation tickets by severity, monitor ticket trends over time, track remediation efforts by the team, and ensure compliance goals are met.

To create this dashboard from a template, go to Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > Violation Tickets Dashboard. To learn more, see [Using Dashboard Templates](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-dashboard-templates).

## Widgets

The charts and tables provide a detailed breakdown of violation tickets categorized by severity, time, and assignee.

- Open Violation Tickets By Severity
- Open Violation Tickets Over Time
- Open Violation Tickets Progress Over Time
- Remediation Percentage by Assignee

The pie chart summarizes open violation tickets based on their severity level. Each color-coded sector represents a specific severity level, allowing you to quickly assess the risk.

The legend provides details for each category, including the category name, the count of open violation tickets, and the relative percentage of the total ticket volume.

The risk levels displayed on the pie chart are:

- Critical (maroon): The total open violation tickets with the highest risk level.
- High (red): The total open violation tickets with significant risk.
- Medium (orange): The total open violation tickets with moderate risk.
- Low (yellow): The total open violation tickets with low risk.

See image.

[Image: Open Violation Tickets By Severity]

The time-series line chart provides a historical overview of open violation tickets, helping you identify trends in ticket resolution or accumulation over a specific period.

A downward slope confirms that the team is meeting compliance goals, while an upward or static trend serves as a prompt to adjust resources or investigate technical blockers in the remediation pipeline.

See image.

Click a date on the timeline, and click **View Items** to see a detailed list of all open violation tickets for the specific date.

See image.

The multi-series line chart tracks the history of open violation tickets by severity level. The chart tracks three distinct severity levels, each represented by a color-coded line.

This visualization allows you to analyze the velocity and priority of a team's remediation efforts, and monitor the security posture over a timeline to facilitate data-driven decision-making.

Horizontal lines indicate no new tickets were opened, and no existing tickets were closed. A downward slope suggests that remediation processes are effective across all severity levels.

The risk levels displayed on the multi-series line chart are:

- Critical (maroon): Open violation tickets with the highest risk level.
- High (red): Open violation tickets with significant risk.
- Medium (orange): Open violation tickets with moderate risk.
- Low (yellow): Open violation tickets with low risk.

See image.

Click a date on the timeline, and click **View Items** to see a detailed list of all open violation tickets for the specific date and severity level.

See image.

The table provides a month-over-month performance comparison of how teams and individuals resolve violation tickets. The table lists the individuals or teams currently responsible for the violation tickets, the number of open versus closed violation tickets assigned to them, and the rate of ticket closure. This allows you to track the progress of ticket resolution, identify bottlenecks in the remediation workflow, and ensure accountability across teams.

See image.

[Image: List of violation ticket records over time]

[Image: Open Violation Tickets Over Time]

[Image: Open Violation Tickets Progress Over Time]

[Image: List of open violation tickets progress over time]

[Image: Table showing violation remediation metrics by assignee]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/viewing-zscaler-secops-status-board","lastmod":"2025-10-30T13:35Z","nid":"1532848"} -->
## Viewing the Zscaler SecOps Status Board

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-zscaler-secops-status-board
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Getting Started > Viewing the Zscaler SecOps Status Board
- Last modified: 2025-10-30T13:35Z
- Summary: How to view information in the Zscaler SecOps status board.

To view the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) status board, refer to the [status page](https://avalorstatus.statuspage.io/). The status board presents historic and current incidents in the SecOps platform.

On the status board, you can perform the following actions:

- Report Issues
- Subscribe to Updates and Feeds
- View Current Status
- View Incident History and Historical Uptime

If you're a SecOps user and you've encountered an issue with the platform or one of its apps, you can report it to the SecOps team.

To report an issue, click **Submit a request** at the top right of the page.

You can subscribe to incident updates by email, phone, and Slack, and to the status board's Atom and RSS feeds.

To subscribe to updates:

1. Click **Subscribe to Updates**at the top right of the page.
2. Click the icon of your preferred update method, and follow the onscreen instructions. See image.

The SecOps platform's current status presents incidents in the last 90 days by region (US, EU), and each region is broken down into additional components:

- Platform
- Data Ingestion
- Query Engine
- UVM App
- Detections App (only for US)

The SecOps platform reports past incidents and historical uptime.

## Incidents

You can view past incident descriptions in 90-day increments.

To view incident history, choose one of the following methods:

- On the **Current Status** page, scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Incident History**.
- On the **Uptime** page, click the **Incident**tab.

## Uptime

You can view historical uptime in 90-day increments and by one of the following components:

- Platform
- Data Ingestion
- Query Engine
- UVM App
- Detections App (only for US)

To view uptime history, choose one of the following methods:

- On the **Current Status** page, click **View historical uptime** in the top right.
- On the **Incidents** page, click the **Uptime**tab.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/what-zscaler-security-operations","lastmod":"2026-05-01T07:06Z","nid":"1532845"} -->
## What Is Zscaler Security Operations?

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/what-zscaler-security-operations
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Getting Started > What Is Zscaler Security Operations?
- Last modified: 2026-05-01T07:06Z
- Summary: Information on the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform.

Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) is a unified approach to security that integrates proactive and reactive measures to enhance an organization's overall security posture. It focuses on bridging the gap between traditional exposure management and threat management, creating a cohesive strategy for identifying, prioritizing, and responding to cyber risks. This comprehensive view helps accelerate incident response, improve operational efficiency, and simplify compliance efforts.

## Key Features and Benefits

Zscaler SecOps provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Integrate Zscaler SecOps and third-party data for rich context, providing a comprehensive view of your security landscape.
- Offer automated workflows for remediation and updates.
- Provide real-time visibility into security posture and metrics.

There are two applications in the Zscaler SecOps platform:

- Asset Exposure Management (AEM) enables organizations to collect and manage asset data from various sources to track asset inventory and coverage. It allows organizations to understand their attack surface, create policies, and track and remediate policy violations to reduce overall risk.
- Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) provides a single platform for managing vulnerabilities, simplifying the process of identifying and remediating security risks.

The Zscaler SecOps platform natively integrates External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities to automatically discover, inventory, and monitor internet-facing assets and detect their associated risk findings. This scanned asset and finding information is automatically merged with the context-rich data and capabilities of AEM and UVM to provide comprehensive asset visibility and enriched security insights, helping organizations secure their assets and remediate risks.

## How Does Zscaler SecOps Work?

Zscaler SecOps operates on a robust data fabric for security that centralizes and transforms disparate security data. Supported by machine learning and AI, the fabric harmonizes, deduplicates, correlates, and enriches information from various sources, including Zscaler telemetry and third-party tools. The clean, contextualized data leads to more accurate and informative security outcomes. These insights power exposure management solutions, such as AEM and UVM, enabling organizations to understand and address asset risk, prioritize vulnerabilities, and effectively quantify overall cyber risk.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/zscaler-secops-public-ip-addresses","lastmod":"2025-10-30T13:25Z","nid":"1532847"} -->
## Zscaler SecOps Public IP Addresses

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/zscaler-secops-public-ip-addresses
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Getting Started > Zscaler SecOps Public IP Addresses
- Last modified: 2025-10-30T13:25Z
- Summary: A list of public IP addresses used by the Zscaler Security Operations platform and its applications (e.g., UVM, AEM) for allowlisting when configuring integrations with the platform.

To ensure seamless connectivity and uninterrupted access to essential resources, you can allowlist the public IP addresses used by outgoing traffic from the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform and its applications (e.g., UVM, AEM). These IP addresses serve as the source for all egress traffic originating from the Zscaler tenant.

Add the following IP addresses associated with your instance's region to your firewall's allowlist to ensure uninterrupted access to the required resources.

| **Region** | **IP Addresses** |
| --- | --- |
| **US** | 3.137.47.190/32 3.15.110.62/32 3.129.232.141/32 |
| **EU** | The recommended IP addresses listed in [Zscaler Hub IP Addresses](https://config.zscaler.com/zscalertwo.net/hubs) |

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-account-onboarding","lastmod":"2026-07-10T09:54Z","nid":"1541174"} -->
## About Account Onboarding

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-account-onboarding
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > About Account Onboarding
- Last modified: 2026-07-10T09:54Z
- Summary: Information about onboarding accounts in the AI Security Admin Portal.

Account onboarding in AI Security enables organizations to establish a secure, governed foundation for managing and monitoring AI application usage. By integrating user identities, cloud environments, and security policies from the outset, organizations gain immediate visibility and control over how AI tools are accessed and used across the enterprise.

AI Security continuously monitors and scans the onboarded accounts for sensitive data and vulnerabilities, and generates [issues](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) based on data security [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies) violations. AI Security supports the onboarding of [Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization) accounts, [Microsoft Azure](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant) subscriptions, [Google Cloud Platform (GCP)](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization) projects, and SaaS applications like [Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-copilot-studio-tenant).

Account Onboarding in AI Security provides the following benefits:

- Gain a unified view of all AI application usage across the organization, including SaaS applications and cloud environments.
- Detect misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, potential threats that could lead to data breach.
- Respond to security risks and take necessary action to prevent data breach.
- Detect and restrict unauthorized AI applications automatically.

## About the Account Onboarding Page

On the Account Onboarding page (Administration> Account Onboarding), you can do the following:

1. View metrics from the following perspectives:
  - **Total Environments:** The total number of environments that have been added and configured across all integrations.
  - **Healthy Integrations:** Integrations for which all required permission checks and access validations have passed.
  - **Unhealthy Integrations:** Integrations where one or more permission checks, access validations, or configuration checks have failed or reported issues.
  - **Pending Configuration:** Integrations with one or more environments that are added but still require configuration to be completed.
2. Click **+ Add New** to start onboarding Cloud Providers or SaaS Platforms.
3. Search for a specific integration in the Configured Integrations table.
4. Apply filters to view specific data.
5. Show or hide columns of the table.
6. Show or hide filters of the table
7. View a list of accounts that are onboarded. For each account you can view the following:
  - **Integration Alias:** The display name for the integration as configured in the system. Click the integration name to view additional details.
  - **Provider:** The service the integration connects to, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, Copilot Studio, etc.
  - **Accounts:** The number of accounts, tenants, or environments onboarded under the integration.
  - **Business Units:** The organizational groups associated with the integration.
  - **Health Status:** The overall integration health based on validation checks, e.g., Passed, Pending, Needs Attention, etc.
  - **Orchestrator Config Status:** The configuration state of the orchestrator or connector used to run the integration, e.g., Successfully Configured, Pending Configuration, Needs Attention).
  - **Issues:** A summary or count of detected problems affecting the integration, e.g., failed checks, missing permissions, configuration errors.
  - **Actions:** Available actions are as follows:
    - **Cloud Service Providers**: Modify Integration or Delete Integration.
    - **SaaS Applications**: Add New Account/Environment, Update Credentials, or Delete Integration.

[Image: The Account Onboarding page displays a summary of all the accounts onboarded and so on.]

- While the onboarding process is in progress or if AI Security has encountered issues, you can view the issue or paused step and resume onboarding.
- When the onboarding process is completed successfully, you can view the following tabs:
  - **Overview**: The onboarding status and the orchestrator details.
  - **Subscriptions**, **Projects**, **Accounts,**or **Environments** (based on the cloud account or SaaS application): [Details](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarded-account-details) of the onboarded cloud account.
  - **Issues**: The issues encountered while onboarding.
  - **Roles and Templates**: The roles created while onboarding and templates generated by AI Security.
- Manage the cloud accounts:
  - **Monitoring & Autodetection**: Add new accounts to the monitoring scope and enable autodetection.
  - **Business Units Mapping**: Assign a different [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units) to the account.
  - **On Demand Validation**: Validate the [onboarded accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/validating-cloud-accounts).
  - **Manage Regions**: Select regions that must be monitored and scanned or configure regions to deploy scanning resources for custom network configuration.
  - **Manage Custom Tags**: Add, edit, or delete custom tags.
  - **Manage Notification Emails**: Add email addresses of the recipient to be notified of any configuration or permissions issues while onboarding.
  - **Managing Orchestrator Network** (Custom): Configure the [orchestrator network](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-orchestrator-network) (applicable only if the **AI Security** **Connection Status** is failed). To learn more, see [Viewing Orchestrator Status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-orchestrator-status).
  - **Configure New Orchestrator**(Zscaler): Change the orchestrator account.
  - **Delete Account**: Delete or offboard an account.
- **Manage SaaS Applications**:
  - **Add New Account/Environment:** Add new account or environment.
  - **Update Credentials:** Update credentials.
  - **Delete Integration:** Delete integration.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-agents","lastmod":"2026-06-09T21:06Z","nid":"1540893"} -->
## About AI Assets - Agents

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-agents
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > AI Assets > About AI Assets - Agents
- Last modified: 2026-06-09T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the AI Assets - Agents in the AI Security Admin Portal

Agents are AI-powered assistants that can understand your goal, decide the next best step, and use connected tools and data sources to complete tasks on your behalf. Unlike a basic chatbot that only answers questions, an agent can take action, such as retrieving information, running checks, generating outputs, and coordinating multistep workflows while keeping you in control.

In Zscaler's AI Security, agents are AI orchestration workflows or chatbots that can connect LLMs, enterprise data sources (knowledge), and tools, including agents to complete tasks or workflows. Because agents can invoke tools and interact with sensitive resources, they are treated as first-class AI assets that need dedicated discovery, inventory, and risk visibility across cloud and code environments.

The AI Assets - Agents page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Find and inventory agents discovered across environments (e.g., cloud services and code repositories) in one place.
- View an agent’s overall risk level, rolled up from its most severe issues, along with warning indicators and Asset Risk labels that flag adverse conditions.
- Understand what the agent connects to, such as tools, agents, data sources, and identities with access to estimate potential blast radius.
- Prioritize, review and remediate by focusing on agents with the highest-risk issues and broadest access paths.
- Support lifecycle decisions based on discovery status and risk.

## About the AI Assets - Agents Page

On the AI Assets - Agents page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Agents), you can do the following:

1. Filter by **Business Units**.
2. View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of the agents:
  - **Agents by Risk**: View the distribution of agents by severity of risk, categorized as **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low,** or**Unknown.**
  - **Agents by Status**: View the distribution of governance status of each agent, categorized as **Sanctioned**, **Unsanctioned**, or **Pending**.
  - **Agents with Access to Sensitive Data**: View the number of agents that can access sensitive data and view the number of agents that are publicly exposed.
3. Search for a specific agent.
4. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/using-filters) to view specific data.
5. View a list of agents which were discovered. For each agent you can view:
  - **Name**: The name of the agent. Click the agent's name to view additional details.
  - **Type**: The type of server, i.e., **Remote**or **Local**.
  - **Risk Level**: The risk level of the agent based on the risk score.
  - **Asset Risk**: The security posture assigned to the identity (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.). Hover over the label to see the description of each posture.
  - **Environment**: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.
  - **Source**: Indicates the specific location or service where the agent was discovered, stored, or hosted.
  - **Risk Score**: Indicates the overall severity rating that indicates how risky a specific agent is. Risk levels are classified as **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low.**
  - **Last Discovered:**The timestamp of when the agent was discovered.
  - **Status**: The approval status of the agents, e.g., **Pending**, **Sanctioned**, or **Unsanctioned**.

- **General Information**: Information such as type, path, source, account ID, account name, organization ID, and region. Click **More Details** for a graphical view.
- **Risk Level**: Indicates the potential blast radius if this agent is compromised. The rating is based on capabilities such as system command execution, file write or delete access, credential storage or access, and outbound (external) network calls.
- **Lifecycle**: Timeline showing the stages an AI model goes through from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates, with timestamps for key milestones.
- The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
  - Graph View
  - Data Security (visible if data is filtered by sensitive data)
  - Issues

A graph shows the connections between the agents and associated components. Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.

Use this tab to view information about the sensitive files that were discovered.

- **Matched Files**: The number of files that matched the DLP engines.
- **Triggers**: Number of alerts raised for the resource.
- **DLP Engines**: The DLP engines that match sensitive records.
- **DLP Dictionaries**: The dictionaries associated with the DLP engines.
- **Document Categories**: The category of document detected in the resource.
- **Document Types**: The number of documents detected in the resource.

You can do the following in the data security table:

- Search for a specific sensitive file.
- Filter data by **Linked Datastore**, **Sensitive DLP Engines**, **DLP Engines**, **DLP Dictionaries**, **Database**, or **Document Type**.
- View a list of sensitive files which were discovered. For each sensitive file you can view:
  - File Name
  - File Path
  - File Size
  - DLP Engines
  - DLP Dictionaries
  - Document Types
  - Last Completed Scan
  - Created Date

Use this tab to view a list of issues that were discovered. For each issue, you can view:

- **Issue ID**: The unique identifier for the issue.
- **Policy Name**: The policy title.
- **Policy Category**: The threat category, e.g., public exposure, data loss, etc., that the policy belongs to.
- **Risk Level**: The risk level, i.e., **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**.
- **Cloud Account**: The unique identifier of the cloud account in which the model is located.
- **Created On**: The date and time the issue was created.
- **Last Updated**: The date and time the issue was last updated.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-mcp-servers","lastmod":"2026-07-10T05:29Z","nid":"1540822"} -->
## About AI Assets - MCP Servers

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-mcp-servers
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > AI Assets > About AI Assets - MCP Servers
- Last modified: 2026-07-10T05:29Z
- Summary: Information about the AI Assets - MCP Servers in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The AI Assets MCP Servers page in AI Security Admin Portal provides a centralized inventory of discovered Model Context Protocol (MCP) server instances so you can understand where MCP is present in your environment and assess the potential security exposure introduced by server capabilities (e.g., file system access, network access, code execution) and other risk indicators. At a high level, it shows each MCP instance’s resource name, where it was detected (resource types such as VMs or containers and the resource path), programming language, and an overall risk score and risk level. It also includes a governance-style status, e.g., Approved, Disapproved, or Pending Review.

MCP servers provide a standardized way to extend language models with real-world capabilities while keeping integrations consistent and reusable.

The AI Assets - MCP Servers Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Reduce one-off connector work by standardizing how tools, prompts, and resources are exposed to models.
- Support deploying the same MCP server patterns across multiple AI applications and environments.
- Make model-to-tool interactions more explicit (for example, defined tools/resources), which helps governance when properly inventoried and reviewed.
- Reduce user risk by supporting governance of approved MCP servers and limiting unsafe or noncompliant integrations.

## About the AI Assets - MCP Servers Page

On the AI Assets MCP Servers page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - MCP Servers), you can do the following:

1. Filter by **Business Units**.
2. View metrics from the following perspectives:
  - **MCP Servers by Risk**: View the distribution of MCP servers' potential blast radius if the MCP server is compromised. Ratings are categorized as **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**.
  - **MCP Serverss by Status**: View the distribution of governance status of each MCP server, categorized as **Sanctioned**, **Unsanctioned**, or **Pending**.
  - **MCP Servers by Type**: View the distribution of the MCP server based on the deployment type.
3. Search for a specific MCP.
4. Click **Export**to export the data and download the report as an Excel file.
5. Show or hide columns.
6. Show or hide filters.
7. Apply filters to view specific data.
8. View a list of MCP Servers which were discovered. For each MCP server you can view:
  - **Name**: The name of the MCP server. Click the MCP Server name to view additional details.
  - **Type**: The type of server, i.e., **Remote**or **Local**.
  - **Environment**: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.
  - **Source**: Indicates the specific location or service where the AI model was discovered, stored, or hosted.
  - **Asset Risk**: Indicates the overall measure of how much security risk an MCP server introduces to the environment where it runs, based on what the server can do.
  - **Risk Score**: Indicates the overall severity rating that indicates how risky a specific MCP server is. Risk levels are classified as **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**,
  - **Last Discovered:**The timestamp of when the MCP server was discovered.
  - **Status**: The approval status of the MCP server, e.g., **Pending**, **Sanctioned**, or **Unsanctioned**.

- **General Information**: Information such as type, path, source, account ID, account name, organization ID, and region. Click **More Details** for a graphical view.
- **Risk Level**: Indicates the potential blast radius if this MCP server is compromised. The rating is based on capabilities such as system command execution, file write or delete access, credential storage or access, and outbound (external) network calls. Critical means the server can execute commands, modify files, handle credentials, and contact external services. Low means the server is primarily read-only, with no system-level access.
- **Lifecycle**: Timeline showing the stages an AI model goes through from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates, with timestamps for key milestones.
- The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
  - Graph View
  - Tools
  - Prompts

A graph shows the connections between the MCP Server, its client, and associated components such as, tools, prompts, resources, code repository, dependencies, API calls, network connections, file systems, etc. Red warning icons indicate issues within specific components, providing users with a clear map for assessing and resolving vulnerabilities.

The graphs also include attack paths that show how the resource is compromised either through public exposure, malware, by an IAM entity (user, service, role) with access privileges, vulnerabilities, etc. This information helps you analyze the issues in detail and remediate them immediately.

You can click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.

Use this tab to view tools information:

1. Search by tool name.
2. View a list of tools which were discovered. For each tool, you can view:
  - **Name:** The name of the tool.
  - **Description:**A human-readable summary of what the tool does and why it exists.
  - **Parameters:**Structured inputs a user (or client) sends when invoking an MCP tool. They define what the tool needs to run and often determine its security impact (for example, which file, host, or URL it can touch).
  - **File Access:**Indicates whether the tool has file access or not.
  - **Network Access:**Indicates whether the tool has network access or not.
  - **Code Execution:**Indicates whether the tool can execute code or system commands
  - **Process Access:**Indicates if the tool can view, start, stop, signal, or attach to running processes (for example, enumerate processes, kill processes, read process info, or interact with process memory or output).
  - **File Path:**The file-system path(s) the tool can access or that the tool targets (often tied to traversal risk).

Use this tab to view prompt information. In an MCP setup, prompts are the instructions provided to the model, and, indirectly, to tools, that shape behavior and outputs. They’re typically captured in two primary types:

- **MCP Prompts**: Instruction text provided to an MCP-enabled model to guide how it should respond and how it should use MCP tools. It typically includes the system prompt (rules and guardrails for the session) and the user prompt (the user’s task request), and may also include additional context such as tool descriptions, parameters, and prior conversation.
- **System Prompts**: Instructions that define the model’s role, boundaries, safety rules, and operating constraints (for example, what the assistant must/never do, tone, and tool-use rules). Applied across the session and generally not user-editable.
- **User Prompts**: The end user’s request or question. It provides the task intent and context (for example, Summarize this incident report or Generate Terraform for this configuration). It can change every turn and is user-controlled.

- **Environment:** Returns data about the environment where the MCP server was discovered, eg. AWS, Azure, or GCP.
- **Regions:** Returns MCP servers for the selected regions. You can exclude regions as required.
- **Accounts:** Returns results from selected cloud accounts.
- **Type:** Returns MCP servers based on whether they are remote or local.
- **Source:** Returns data based on the source from which MCP servers originate, such as AWS Bedrock Agent.
- **Asset Risk:** Returns results that match the selected filter criteria. Risk signals may include:
  - Execution capabilities
  - File deletion operations
  - Directory traversal
  - External network access
  - Credential storage/handling
  - Processing of sensitive data (for example, PII)
- **Risk Score:** Returns data based on the overall severity rating that indicates how risky a specific MCP server is.
- **Status:** Returns data based on the current status of the MCP server.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-models","lastmod":"2026-07-10T03:45Z","nid":"1540775"} -->
## About AI Assets - Models

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-models
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > AI Assets > About AI Assets - Models
- Last modified: 2026-07-10T03:45Z
- Summary: Information about the AI Assets - Models in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The AI Assets Models page in AI Security Admin Portal is a centralized model inventory that provides a unified view of all custom, managed, and unmanaged models across your environments, enabling standardized governance through clear classification and sanctioning. By surfacing benchmark-based risk signals and sensitive data exposure indicators, it allows teams to prioritize remediation and make informed data protection decisions. This shared visibility streamlines investigation and triage via granular search and filters, ensuring that security, governance, and engineering teams remain aligned on approved models and operational actions.

The AI Assets - Models Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Maintain an inventory of detected LLMs across the enterprise, including foundation models, custom (fine-tuned) models, and unmanaged or open-source models, e.g., Hugging Face or Ollama.
- See where each model was discovered, when it was last discovered and updated, and its associated risk and security signals.
- Classify models as assets and apply a governance status, e.g., Sanctioned, Unsanctioned, or Pending, where supported.
- Prioritize review and remediation using benchmark-based model risk signals and, when available, supply-chain risk.
- Identify sensitive data exposure by viewing DLP indicators, e.g., top classified data types and engines associated with model usage.
- Provide shared visibility so security, governance, and engineering teams can align on approved models, exceptions, and next steps as the model landscape changes.

## About the AI Assets - Models Page

On the AI Assets Models page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Models), you can do the following:

1. Filter by **Business Units**.
2. View metrics from the following perspectives:
  - **Models by Risk**: View distribution of the model's vulnerability to adversarial exploits, such as prompt injection, jailbreaking, and unauthorized data extraction. Ratings are categorized as **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**. This score specifically measures the model's attack resistance rather than the severity of known open issues.
  - **Models by Status**: View the distribution of governance status of each model, categorized as **Sanctioned**, **Unsanctioned**, or **Pending**.
  - **Models by Subtype**: View the distribution of the model's origin. The categories are as follows:
    - **Foundation**: A vendor-provided, pre-trained base model, e.g., an LLM or embedding model and used as-is.
    - **Free-Tuning**: A foundation model trained further on your organization’s data for specific tasks.
    - **Imported**: A model introduced from an external source, e.g., third-party model registry, open-source repository, or another account or tenant.
    - **Unknown**: The subtype could not be determined from the available metadata.
    - **Others**: Models that do not match the listed subtypes.
3. Search for a specific model.
4. Click **Export**to export the data and download the report as an Excel file.
5. Show or Hide columns.
6. Show or Hide filters.
7. Apply filters to view specific data.
8. View a list of AI models that were discovered. For each AI model you can view:
  - **Name**: The name of the AI model. Click the model name to view additional details.
  - **Type & Subtype**: The AI model type, e.g., Managed Model, Unmanaged Model, Custom Model, etc. and the model subtype, e.g., Fine-tuning.
  - **Environment**: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.
  - **Source**: Indicates the specific location or service where the AI model was discovered, stored, or hosted.
  - **Status**: The model's governance status, e.g., **Pending**, **Sanctioned**,or **Unsanctioned**.
  - **Sensitive Data**: The DLP engines used for classification and the document types detected in model-related data.
  - **Model Risk**: The model's benchmark-based average risk score, e.g., **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **Unknown**.
  - **Model Supply Chain Risk**: The severity rating from supply chain analysis, e.g., **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **Unknown**.

- **General Information**: Information such as region, environment, type, subtype, account ID, and account name. Click **More Details** to view a graphical summary.
- **Model Score**: Risk of the model being exploited through adversarial attacks like prompt injection, jaikbreaks, and data extraction. Benchmark-based risk score is shown only when a benchmark has been run. If the model type is unmanaged and if the risk score is greater than 0, another tab, Model Security, is visible. To view further details, click **View Model Benchmark**.
- **Lifecycle**: Timeline of key milestones from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates.
- The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
  - Graph View
  - Issues
  - Model Supply Chain Risk
  - Model Security (Only for unmanaged models)
  - Usage (Only for AWS managed and custom models)
  - Top 10 Users (Only for AWS managed and custom models)

The graphs consist of interactive nodes that provide contextual information, e.g., cloud account name, region, type, account ID, account name, file path, risk score, about the primary AI model and the associated secondary resources.

The graphs also include attack paths that show how the resource is compromised either through public exposure, malware, by an IAM entity (user, service, role) with access privileges, vulnerabilities, etc. This information helps you analyze the issues in detail and remediate them immediately.

Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.

The risk assessment results for an unmanaged AI model summarize the risk assessment across the following categories:

- **Risk Score**: Indicates the composite supply chain risk for this model on a scale of 0 to 100.
- **Severity**: Indicates the severity category, i.e., **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**derived by rolling up the underlying numeric risk score.
- **Documentation**: Checks the license type and library framework of the AI model.
- **Risk Indicators**: Evaluates the AI model for specific risks like unsafe files or missing Safetensors file formats.
- **Files**: Analyzes the AI model file formats and security scan results (scanned by Hugging Face) to check for Safetensors file formats, config.json, and README. Unsafe, Caution, and Suspicious labels are assigned to suspicious files.

You can view model security details in the following sections:

- **Performance Summary**: Indicates the benchmark results across four quality dimensions, i.e., Security, Safety, Hallucinations, and Business Alignment. You can also view details in the following tabs:
  - Overall
  - No System Prompt
  - Basic System Prompt
  - Hardened System Prompt
- **Test Results Drilldown**: You can view the overall probe cards displaying the cumulative scores of the model.
- **Compare**: Click the **Compare** tab and select the models you want to review to evaluate several models for your use case. The comparison view shows side-by-side performance across multiple categories and system prompt configurations, so you can quickly choose the best option. To learn more, see **About Model Security**.

View a list of issues that were discovered. For each issue, you can view:

- **Issue ID**: The unique identifier for the issue.
- **Policy Name**: The policy title.
- **Policy Category**: The threat category, e.g., public exposure, data loss, etc., that the policy belongs to.
- **Risk Level**: The risk level, i.e., Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
- **Cloud Account**: The unique identifier of the cloud account in which the model is located.
- **Created On**: The date and time the issue was created.
- **Last Updated**: The date and time the issue was last updated.

- **Environment:** Returns data about the environment where the AI model was discovered based on your filter selections, such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
- **Type:** Returns data about the category of the AI model based on your filter selections. The following options are supported:
  - **Managed:** AI models that are fully managed by a cloud service provider (CSP), such as AWS Bedrock or Azure OpenAI.
  - **Unmanaged:** AI models that are deployed and managed independently, outside a CSP's managed offering.
  - **Custom:** AI models that are built and trained in-house by the organization.
  - **Registry Model:** AI models that are sourced from a model registry or public repository, such as Hugging Face or a container registry.
- **Subtype:**Returns data about the specific classification within the model type based on your filter selections, providing a more granular view of the model's function or architecture.
- **Source:**Returns data about the origin of the AI model based on your filter selections, such as whether it was built in-house, sourced from a third-party provider, or obtained from a public model repository.
- **Status:** Returns data about the current operational state of the AI model based on your filter selections, such as whether it is pending, sanctioned, or unsanctioned.
- **Sensitive Data:** Returns data about whether the AI model has access to or processes sensitive data based on your filter selections, as detected by DLP engines or document types, such as personally identifiable information (PII), financial data, or health records.
- **Model Risk:**Model Risk Indicates the risk level associated with the AI model based on factors such as known vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or non-compliance with security policies. The following risk levels are supported:
  - Critical: The model has severe vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that require immediate attention.
  - High: The model has significant vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that pose a considerable security risk.
  - Medium: The model has moderate vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that should be addressed in a timely manner.
  - Low: The model has minor vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that present a minimal security risk.
  - Unknown: The risk level of the model could not be determined due to insufficient data or incomplete scanning.
- **Model Supply Chain Risk:** Returns data about the risk associated with the AI model's supply chain, including the libraries, dependencies, and third-party components used to build or run the model.

View a timeline showing the usage activity of the AI model over time. The following details are available in the table:

- **Invoker Principal:** The principal entity, such as a user, role, or service account, that invoked the AI model.
- **Invoker User Name:**The username associated with the entity that invoked the AI model.
- **Last Seen:**The most recent date and time the AI model was invoked or detected.
- **Invocation Count:** The total number of times the AI model has been invoked.

View a list of the top 10 invokers associated with the AI model. For each invoker, the following details are available:

- **Invoker Principal:** The principal entity, such as a user, role, or service account, that invoked the AI model.
- **Invoker User Name:** The username associated with the entity that invoked the AI model.
- **Last Seen:**The most recent date and time the AI model was invoked or detected.
- **Invocation Count:** The total number of times the AI model has been invoked.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies","lastmod":"2026-06-18T03:34Z","nid":"1540840"} -->
## About AI Posture Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > AI Posture Policies & Data Classification > AI Posture Policies > About AI Posture Policies
- Last modified: 2026-06-18T03:34Z
- Summary: Information about the AI posture policies that are defined and implemented in AI Security.

AI Posture policies are queries or rules that AI Security define to protect your cloud resources from potential threats and improve your cloud security posture. Policies provide guidelines for managing and protecting your organization's sensitive data and ensuring it is stored securely and only shared with authorized users.

AI Security scans the resources against the policies enabled in your Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, Azure subscriptions, and Google Cloud Storage; identifies where the sensitive data is located, vulnerabilities such as any misconfigurations, presence of malware, or if the resource is publicly exposed to the internet; and potential breach possibilities. AI Security generates [issues](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) that help you prioritize an incident and quickly remediate the issue. The policies are grouped by [threat categories](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/threat-categories).

AI Security offers predefined policies that are aligned with industry standard cybersecurity and compliance benchmarks such as [NIST](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework), [GDPR](https://gdpr-info.eu/), [PCI](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/standards/), etc. You can create [custom policies](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/creating-custom-policies) to meet your organization's requirements. AI Security also provides predefined policies that use advanced options to scan the data.

AI Posture policies provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- View all the policies offered by AI Security.
- Gain AI posture overview based on whether the policies are passing or failing for your resources.
- Create custom security policies to meet your organization's compliance requirements.
- Enable or disable policies on resources.

## About the Policy Page

On the Policy page (Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies), you can do the following:

1. [Apply filters to view specific data](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. [Add additional filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
3. Search for a specific policy.
4. [Add a custom policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/creating-custom-policies).
5. View the policy details. For each policy, you can view:
  - **Policy Name**: The policy title.
  - **Severity**: The severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) of the policy.
  - **Policy Source**: Whether the policy is a predefined or a custom policy.
  - **Primary Resource Type**: The type of resource on which the policy is applied.
  - **Last Updated**: The date and time the policy was last updated.
  - **Cloud**: The cloud type in which the resource is located.
  - **ID**: The unique identifier for the policy.
  - **Created**: The date and time the policy was created.
  - **Policy Category**: The category (Public Exposure, Data Loss, etc.) to which this policy belongs.
  - **Policy Status**: The status (Enabled or Disabled) of the policy.
6. Select multiple policies to either enable or disable them. See image.
7. Click the policy name to view additional details. To learn more, see [Viewing Policy Details](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-policy-details).
8. Sort the column data.
9. View the list of policy categories associated with the policy.
10. [Enable or disable the policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies).
11. Select any of the following actions:
  - **Enable**: [Enable a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies). This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
  - **Disable**: [Disable a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies). This option is available only when the policy is enabled.
  - **Clone**: [Clone a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies).
  - **Change Severity**: Change the severity level of the policy. This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
  - **Edit**: [Edit a custom policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies). This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
  - **Delete**: [Delete a custom policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies). This option is available only when the policy is disabled. You cannot edit, delete, or change the severity level for predefined policies.
12. [Show or hide the columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).

[Image: The list of policies and various actions that can be performed on them.]

[Image: Enable or disable multiple policies simultaneously]
