<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-ai-software-libraries","lastmod":"2026-06-08T21:06Z","nid":"1540213"} -->
## About AI Resources - AI Software Libraries

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-ai-software-libraries
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > AI Resources > About AI Resources - AI Software Libraries
- Last modified: 2026-06-08T21:06Z
- Summary: The AI Resources page displays AI models, AI services, and AI Software Libraries in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Software Libraries are the third-party and internal packages that power AI development and runtime, such as frameworks for model training and inference, SDKs for calling LLMs, orchestration or agent frameworks, vector database clients, and supporting utilities. These libraries are a critical part of the AI supply chain as they can introduce vulnerabilities, unsafe capabilities, and license or compliance obligations into AI applications and agent workflows.

Zscaler's AI Security enables tracking of AI software libraries, thereby helping security and platform teams understand what components AI systems rely on, assess exposure, e.g., risky dependencies or outdated versions), and enforce organizational policies for secure and compliant AI deployments.

The AI Resources - AI Software Libraries page provides a tabular view of AI resources that exist across all the onboarded cloud accounts:

The AI Resources - AI Software Libraries page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- See which AI libraries are being used across projects and where they’re deployed.
- Spot restrictive licenses, e.g., GPL and AGPL early to avoid distribution or commercial-use issues.
- Identify high-risk or vulnerable dependencies so you can prioritize upgrades or replacements.
- Pinpoint the library that may be driving a security, policy, or build issue.
- Align teams on approved libraries and versions to reduce drift and surprise changes.
- Produce evidence of license and dependency posture without manual tracking.
- Allows organizations to monitor and evaluate supply chain vulnerabilities associated with their AI-related assets.

## About AI Resources - AI Software Libraries Page

On the AI Resources - AI Software Libraries Page, (AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > AI Software Libraries)**,** you can do the following

1. Filter by **Business Units**.
2. View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your AI software library inventory:
  - **AI Software Libraries by Risk Level**: Distribution of software libraries by their severity across known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and supply chain signals, e.g., **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **None**(no known vulnerabilities and a clean supply chain profile).
  - **AI Software Libraries by Status**: Distribution of the software libraries by their governance status, e.g., **Sanctioned**(reviewed and approved), **Unsanctioned** (reviewed and not approved), or **Unreviewed**(awaiting review).
  - **AI Software Libraries by License Type**: Distribution of AI software libraries by their license types, i.e., the license declared for each library. The license types are as follows:
    - **Permissive License**s: Have fewer redistribution requirements, e.g., AGPL-3.0, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, and MIT.
    - **Copyleft Licenses**: Require derivative works to be open-sourced and may increase compliance risk in commercial deployments, e.g., GPL and AGPL.
3. Search for a specific AI Software Library.
4. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/using-filters) to view specific data.
5. View a list of AI software libraries which were discovered. For each AI library, you can view:
  - **Name & Version**: The name and version of the AI library. Click the library name to view additional details.
  - **Source**: Indicates the specific location or service where the AI library was discovered, stored, or hosted.
  - **Status**: The approval status of the library. The default value is **Pending Review**.
  - **Supply Chain Risk**: The overall risk severity. e.g., **Low**, **Medium**, **High**, **Critical**, or **Unknown**.
  - **Environment**: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., **AWS**, **Azure**, or **GCP**.
  - **Package Type**: The type of AI library, e.g., Data Manipulation & Processing, Large Language Models (LLMs), MLOps Tools, etc.
  - **Vulnerable**: Whether the library has vulnerabilities or not.
  - **License Type**: The licensing terms of the AI library, e.g., Apache-2.0.
  - **Actions**: Click the **Action**icon and select **Sanctioned**or **Unsanctioned**to approve or reject the package's use in the organization.

- **General information**: Information such as package URL, license type, language, package version, and sensitive data.
- **Lifecycle**: Timeline of key milestones from discovery through first scans.
- Graph View
- Supply Chain Risk

The graphs consist of interactive nodes that provide contextual information (e.g., package URL, package type, license type, language, package version, supply chain risk score, and other information like package repository URL, vulnerabilities (CVEs), etc.) about the primary resource and the associated secondary resources.

The graphs also include attack paths that show how the resource is compromised, etc. This information helps you analyze the issues in detail and remediate them immediately.

This tab is enabled and visible only when a Supply Chain Risk Score is available for the model. If the score is not available, the tab remains hidden.

- **Overall Risk Score**: The chart visually represents the overall risk score for the AI software library. The risk scores map to risk levels as follows
  - **Low**: 0–33
  - **Medium**: 34–55
  - **High**: 55–74
  - **Critical**: 75–100
- **Total Categories**: The number of risk categories evaluated for this package. This score is always five and includes, Security, Dependencies, Quality, Maintenance, and Compliance.
- **Categories with Critical Risk**: Number of categories where the category score falls in the critical range, i.e., 75–100 range.
- **Total Issues**: Total number of failed checks across all categories. Each failed check is one issue.
- **Supply Risk Chain Assessment**

The assessment result provides an overview of issues detected in the security techniques applied to the AI library. You can drill down each security technique to view the assigned risk score, risk level, the number of issues detected, current status of the detected issue, and remediation.

- **Security**: Detects issues in the security testing techniques used on the AI package and assigns a risk score.
- **Dependencies**: Detects if the dependencies are pinned to specific versions and updated automatically.
- **Quality**: Detects issues in the code-review and branch protection practices.
- **Maintenance**: Detects issues in the maintenance techniques.
- **Compliance**: Detects compliance issues related to licensing and security policies.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-data-stores","lastmod":"2026-07-13T07:13Z","nid":"1540912"} -->
## About AI Resources - Data Stores

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-data-stores
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > AI Resources > About AI Resources - Data Stores
- Last modified: 2026-07-13T07:13Z
- Summary: Information about the Datastores in the AI Resources page in the AI Security Admin Portal,

AI Resources Data Stores in AI Security provides an inventory of the data stores associated with your AI environment, especially those connected to agents, MCP servers, models, and AI workloads. Use this view to understand what data sources your AI systems can access and to quickly spot configuration and security posture gaps.

The AI Resources - Data Stores Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View AI-related data stores in one place, with key metadata such as tags, account, subscription, or project, and scan status.
- Quickly identify data stores with posture risks, e.g., not encrypted or logging not enabled using posture labels.
- Understand where sensitive data may exist by viewing the top DLP engines triggered by a data store.
- Use Open Graph to explore relationships between data stores and related AI resources (agents, models, workloads) for impact analysis and troubleshooting.
- Track last scanned and scan status to confirm whether findings reflect the latest environment state.

## About the AI Resources - Data Stores Page

On the AI Resources Data Stores page (AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Data Stores), you can do the following:

1. Filter by **Business Units**.
2. View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your data stores:
  - **Data Stores by Risk Level**: Distribution of data stores by severity level among the data store’s open security issues. The severity level is categorized as **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **Unknown**. If the value is **None**, no open issues are currently detected.
  - **Data Stores by Status**: Distribution of the data stores by their governance status, e.g., **Sanctioned**(reviewed and approved), **Unsanctioned**(reviewed and not approved), or **Unreviewed**(awaiting review).
  - **Sensitive Data Exposed to AI**: Distribution of data stores that contain sensitive data, such as PII, PHI, PCI, and are connected to at least one AI model, agent, or workload. Because AI systems can access these data stores, the sensitive data could be unintentionally disclosed or leaked. You can also view the total count of files with sensitive-data matches across those data stores.
3. Search for specific data in the searchable columns.
4. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/using-filters) to view specific data.
5. View the list of data stores. For each data store, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the data store. Click the entity name to view additional details.
  - **Type**: Type of data store.
  - **Environment**: The cloud service provider in which the data store is present.
  - **Risk Level**: The risk level of the data store based on the risk score.
  - **Status**: Governance status of the data store.
  - **Access Type**: The permission level granted to the entity for the selected resource, e.g., **Read**, **Edit**, or **Full Access**.
  - **Source**: Name of the resource type.
  - **Asset Risk**: The security posture assigned to the data store (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.). Hover over the label to see the description of each posture.
  - **Last Completed Scan**: Timestamp of when the last scan was completed.

- **General Information**: Information such as region, type, path, source, account ID, account name, and sensitive data. Click **More Details** for a graphical view.
- **Risk Level**: Indicates the potential blast radius if this data store is compromised. The rating is based on capabilities such as system command execution, file write or delete access, credential storage or access, and outbound (external) network calls.
- **Lifecycle**: Timeline showing the stages an AI agent goes through from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates, with timestamps for key milestones.

The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:

- Graph View
- Data Security
- Issues

The graph for an AI service is a visual representation of the data scan result for the service. It depicts the access path for the AI service (Azure AI Foundry Hub or AWS Bedrock Knowledge Base) where it has access to the storage account containing sensitive data. AI Security also detects if the AI service is publicly exposed to the internet, including the public exposure path, and the list of entities that can access the AI service. These details are helpful to quickly evaluate and remediate the issues, protect the sensitive data, and maintain a strong security posture.

Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.

Use this tab to view details of the sensitive record, including the DLP engines and dictionaries that match the record, the security posture of the record, ID and tags, and the timestamp of the last completed scan as follows:

- **Matched Files**: The number of files that matched the DLP engines.
- **Triggers**: Number of alerts raised for the resource.
- **DLP Engines**: The DLP engines that match sensitive records.
- **DLP Dictionaries**: The dictionaries associated with the DLP engines.
- **Document Categories**: The category of document detected in the resource.
- **Document Types**: The number of documents detected in the resource.

You can do the following in the data security table:

- Search for a specific sensitive file.
- Filter data by **Linked Datastore**, **Sensitive DLP Engines**, **DLP Engines**, **DLP Dictionaries**, **Database**, or **Document Type**.
- View a list of sensitive files which were discovered. For each sensitive file you can view:
  - File Name
  - File Path
  - File Size
  - DLP Engines
  - DLP Dictionaries
  - Document Types
  - Last Completed Scan
  - Created Date

Use this tab to view a list of issues that were discovered. For each issue, you can view:

- **Issue ID**: The unique identifier for the issue.
- **Policy Name**: The policy title.
- **Policy Category**: The threat category, e.g., public exposure, data loss, etc., that the policy belongs to.
- **Risk Level**: The risk level, i.e., **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**.
- **Cloud Account**: The unique identifier of the cloud account in which the model is located.
- **Created On**: The date and time the issue was created.
- **Last Updated**: The date and time the issue was last updated.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-identities","lastmod":"2026-07-30T03:50Z","nid":"1540215"} -->
## About AI Resources - Identities

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-identities
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > AI Resources > About AI Resources - Identities
- Last modified: 2026-07-30T03:50Z
- Summary: Information about the Identities in the AI Resources page in the AI Security Admin Portal, which lists all identities within the cloud environment, along with details about the type and number of data stores that a user has access to.

An identity represents a user, device, application, or service that can access data stores containing sensitive data in the cloud environment. While securing sensitive data, it is crucial to control and manage the permissions assigned to identities, as excessive permissions and insecure configurations could lead to security breaches. AI Security detects identities in all the onboarded cloud accounts (AWS, Azure, and GCP), including managed and unmanaged databases, and Snowflake.

The AI Assets - Identities Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View the identities that can access resources containing sensitive data within your cloud environment.
- View the data stores accessed by an identity.
- View the type of sensitive data accessed by each identity.
- View the security posture of the identity.

## About the AI Resources - Identities Page

On the AI Resources Identities page (AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities), you can do the following:

1. Filter by **Business Units**.
2. View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your identities:
  - **Identities by Type**: Distribution of identity types that access AI resources, eg., AWS IAM User, AWS IAM Role, AWS IAM Policy, GCP Service Account, Azure, etc.
  - **Identities by Status**: Distribution of the software libraries by their governance status, e.g., **Sanctioned**(reviewed and approved), **Unsanctioned**(reviewed and not approved), or **Pending**(awaiting review).
  - **Identities by Risk Posture**: Distribution of identities by security posture risk category, e.g., privileged access, Inactive Certificate, MFA disabled, or Dual Authentication Disabled.
3. Search for specific data in the searchable columns.
4. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/using-filters) to view specific data.
5. View the list of identities. For each identity, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the entity. Click the entity name to view additional details.
  - **Environment**: The cloud service provider in which the identity is present.
  - **Access Type**: The permission level granted to the entity for the selected resource, e.g., **Read**, **Edit**, or **Full Access**.
  - **Source**: Resource type.
  - **Status**: Governance status of the identity.
  - **Risk Posture**: The security posture assigned to the identity (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.). Hover over the label to see the description of each posture.
  - **Last Discovered**: Timestamp when the asset was last updated.

- **General Information:** Information such as type, Source, Account ID, Account Name, Asset Risk, etc. Click **More Details** to view a graphical summary.
- **Lifecycle:** Timeline of key milestones from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates.
- **Graph View:** The graphs consist of interactive nodes that provide contextual information, e.g., cloud account name, region, type, account ID, account name, file path, risk score, about the primary AI identity and the associated secondary resources. The graphs also include attack paths that show how the resource is compromised either through public exposure, malware, by an IAM entity (user, service, role) with access privileges, vulnerabilities, etc. This information helps you analyze the issues in detail and remediate them immediately. Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About AI Security Dashboard

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-security-dashboard
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > Dashboard > About AI Security Dashboard
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the AI Security Dashboard in AI Security Admin Portal

The AI Security Dashboard provides a centralized, at-a-glance view of your organization’s AI application usage and risk posture. From the UI, it brings together key insights, such as which AI apps are being used, usage trends over time, and the most active users or groups, so you can quickly understand where AI is being adopted and where governance may be needed.

The Dashboard is designed to help you move from visibility to action. You can use it to identify sanctioned vs. shadow AI usage, spot unusual spikes in activity, and prioritize AI services that may require tighter controls. The visual widgets and summary cards make it easy to drill into details and pivot to related views (for example, inventory or policy areas) to investigate and respond.

The AI Security Dashboard provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Attain a unified dashboard experience for tracking AI activity, adoption, and risk signals in one place.
- Gain a high-level view of your organization’s traffic to public AI services, including overall volume, active users, and the top departments generating AI traffic.
- Quickly understand adoption and concentration of use, spot unusual spikes, and prioritize governance and controls where AI activity is highest.
- Connects dashboard insights to AI application inventory and AI infrastructure across Gen AI, Embedded AI, and MCP servers, Agents, Apps, etc., helping teams manage AI usage continuously.

## About the AI Security Dashboard Page

On the AI Security Dashboard page, (AI Security > Dashboard), you can view the following widgets and tabs:

1. **Public AI Traffic Overview**: View the total traffic volume and user count for Public AI apps discovered across your organization. You can also see the Top 5 Apps or Top 5 Departments in a bar chart. To drill down, click **Details** to open the [**Public AI- Overview**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-overview) page.
2. **AI Application by Categories:**View the count of newly discovered apps and risky apps. You can also see the distribution of GenAI and Desktop AI apps across your organization in a donut chart. To drill down, click **Details**to open the [**Public AI Inventory**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-gen-ai)page. View top apps across different categories.
3. **AI Assets by Categories:**View the newly discovered assets and risky assets. You can also view the distribution of assets across categories, like Models, MCP servers, Agents, and Apps. Click **Details**to be redirected to the [**AI Assets**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-models) page.
4. The dashboard also displays detailed information in the following tabs:
  - Public AI
  - AI Infrastructure
  - Red Teaming

View the top apps across categories. Use the carousel buttons to switch between the views. Click a category to view further details on the **Public AI - Inventory** page.

Use this tab to view AI-related infrastructure connected to your organization and evaluate its security posture, identify exposed or misconfigured components, and confirm that access controls, logging, and policies are configured correctly. The **Asset Explorer**section displays a visual summary of your AI Inventory across connected cloud accounts and repositories. Each hero node shows the count of the AI Asset Type. You can view data in the following tabs:

- **AI Assets**: Use this tab to view an inventory of AI asset entities—models, MCP servers, agents, and apps, so you can see where AI usage is concentrated and prioritize controls. The central node shows the total AI asset count, and each hero node shows the count for a specific asset type. Select an asset type to view breakdowns by risk level, type, and environment. Click the number to open the corresponding [**AI Asset**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-assets-models) page for more details.
- **AI Resources**: Use this tab to view an inventory of entities involved in AI resource usage, such as data stores, AI software libraries, AI guardrails, identities, and workloads. The central node shows the total AI resource count, and each hero node shows the count for a specific asset type. Select a resource type to view breakdowns by risk level, type, and environment. Click the number to open the corresponding [**AI Resources**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-resources-identities) page for more details.
- **Data Classification for AI**: Use this tab to view an inventory of entities involved in AI data classification categories, such as Source Code, Legal, and Technical. The central node shows the total items and each hero node shows the count for a data classification type. Select a data classification type to view breakdowns by subcategories. Click number to open the corresponding details on the **AI Resources - Workload** page.

Use this tab to view the following information:

- AI Asset Insights
- Untested AI Assets

View a breakdown of AI Assets that have been red-teamed which are categorized based on the following:

- **Health Score**: Displays a segmented view of a health score categorized as critical, low, medium, high, or unknown.
- **Availability**: Displays a segmented view based on whether the asset is internal or customer-facing.

Click **Details**to view details on the [AI Red Teaming Overview](https://help.zscaler.com/secure-ai-apps-infra/about-ai-red-teaming-overview) page.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540157"} -->
## About Business Units

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Role Management > About Business Units
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about business units in the AI Security Admin Portal.

Business units are logical containers for cloud accounts in the AI Security Admin Portal. Business units govern AI Security from a role-based access control (RBAC) perspective. Organizations can control and manage user access to data in their cloud accounts. This controlled access helps alleviate security risks and thereby maintain the security posture of your cloud resources.

You must assign users or user groups to the business units. To learn more, see [About Users](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/about-users).

You can onboard your [cloud accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts) and map them to business units. You can also restrict user access to specific business units. For example, you might want to restrict a specific team to view the alerts only for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Cloud Storage buckets, Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, or restrict partners to view resources only for a certain set of Microsoft Azure subscriptions.

The Business Unit Management page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Manage cloud accounts within the business unit.
- Control what data can be viewed and what tasks can be performed by users on specific sets of cloud accounts.

## About the Business Unit Management Page

On the Business Unit Management page (Administration > Business Unit Management), you can do the following:

1. View the list of business units. For each business unit, you can see:
  - **Business Unit Name**: The name of the business unit. Click to view the cloud accounts that are assigned to this business unit. Click **Manage**to add or delete a cloud account from the [Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts) page. See image.
  - **Account Count**: The number of [cloud accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts) assigned to the business unit.
  - **Created On**: The date and time the business unit was created.
2. Add a business unit. See image.
  1. Click **Add Business Unit**.
  2. In the **Add Business Unit** window, enter a unique name for the business unit.
  3. Click **Create**.
3. Search for specific data in the searchable columns.

## About Cloud Accounts

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > About Cloud Accounts
- Last modified: 2026-06-29T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about onboarding cloud accounts in the AI Security Admin Portal.

Data security is an important aspect of security practices. Organizations need to ensure that data in their cloud accounts is stored, shared, and transferred securely to the right people and services for the right purpose. It is also crucial to know where the data is located, what type of sensitive data (e.g., credit card numbers, login credentials) exists in your cloud accounts, who has access to it, and how secure the data is to prevent any potential data breach.

AI Security continuously monitors and scans the onboarded cloud accounts for sensitive data and vulnerabilities, and generates [issues](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) based on data security [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies) violations. AI Security supports the onboarding of [Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization) accounts, [Microsoft Azure](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant) subscriptions, and [Google Cloud Platform (GCP)](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization) projects.

Onboarding cloud accounts to AI Security provides the following benefits:

- Gain visibility into all the data stored in the cloud accounts.
- Detect misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, potential threats that could lead to data breach.
- Respond to security risks and take necessary action to prevent data breach.

## About the Cloud Accounts Page

On the Cloud Accounts page (Administration> Account Onboarding), you can do the following:

1. View the total number of cloud accounts monitored by AI Security across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
2. Manage the cloud accounts:
  1. **Monitoring & Autodetection**: Add new accounts to the monitoring scope and enable autodetection.
  2. **Business Units Mapping**: Assign a different [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units) to the account.
  3. **Manage Regions**: Select regions that must be monitored and scanned or configure regions to deploy scanning resources for custom network configuration.
  4. **Manage Custom Tags**: Add, edit, or delete custom tags.
  5. **Manage Notification Emails**: Add email addresses of the recipient to be notified of any configuration or permissions issues while onboarding.
  6. **Managing Orchestrator Network** (Custom): Configure the [orchestrator network](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-orchestrator-network) (applicable only if the **AI Security** **Connection Status** is failed). To learn more, see [Viewing Orchestrator Status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-orchestrator-status).
  7. **On Demand Validation**: Validate the [onboarded accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/validating-cloud-accounts).
  8. **Configure New Orchestrator**(Zscaler): Change the orchestrator account.
  9. **Delete Account**: Delete or offboard an account. The following features are specific to cloud service providers:
    1. **AWS**: Manage CloudTrail, Manage Services, Manage Evidence, Manage Data Events.
    2. **Azure**: Change Application Details, Manage Private Endpoint, Manage Services, Manage Evidence.
    3. **GCP**: Update Service Account and Update Private Key.
3. Onboard an AWS organization, GCP organization, or a Microsoft Azure tenant.
4. View the cloud accounts that are onboarded or being onboarded. Select a cloud account to view the following:
  - While the onboarding process is in progress or if AI Security has encountered issues, you can view the issue or paused step and resume onboarding.
  - When the onboarding process is completed successfully, you can view the following tabs:
    - **Overview**: The onboarding status and the orchestrator details.
    - **Subscriptions**, **Projects**, or **Accounts** (based on the cloud account): [Details](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarded-account-details) of the onboarded cloud account.
    - **Issues**: The issues encountered while onboarding.
    - **Roles and Templates**: The roles created while onboarding and templates generated by AI Security.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Data Sensitivity

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-data-sensitivity
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > AI Posture Policies & Data Classification > Data Sensitivity Settings > About Data Sensitivity
- Last modified: 2026-06-10T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the data sensitivity settings in the AI Security Admin Portal and how the DLP engines are used for data classification.

Sensitive data is confidential information such as personally identifiable information (PII), social security numbers, credit card information, financial data, login credentials, etc., that must be protected with strong security controls to prevent data breaches.

Knowing what type of sensitive data exists in your cloud environment and where it is located (regions) is crucial to keep track and monitor this data regularly and ensure the data is secure. An effective method to keep sensitive data secure is through data classification. By classifying sensitive data, you can have more visibility and prioritize the risks, if any, and quickly remediate the issues.

AI Security supports data classification by using robust DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and predefined DLP engines.

You can only view the DLP engines in the AI Security Admin Portal. You can add or modify a DLP engine in Internet & SaaS if you have the necessary permissions. When configuring a predefined or custom engine, you can also combine dictionaries with Boolean operators to create logical expressions.

Defining the data sensitivity provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Classify sensitive data based on the level of sensitivity and risk.
- View the DLP engines and dictionaries that are used by AI Security for data classification.
- Manage the sensitivity setting for DLP engines.

## About the Data Classification Settings Page

On the Data Classification Settings page (Administration > Data Sensitivity), you can do the following:

1. Create and manage DLP Engines. This option is visible to users with permissions to view or edit the DLP Dictionaries & Engines.
2. View the list of DLP engines that are synced from Internet & SaaS. For each DLP engine, you can view:
  1. **DLP Engine Name**: The name of the DLP engine.
  2. **Description**: The description of the DLP engine.
  3. **Engine Type**: The type (Predefined or Custom) of DLP engine.
  4. **Last Modified**: The date and time the DLP engine was last modified.
  5. **Enabled**: The toggle that indicates whether the DLP engine is active.
  6. **Sensitive**: The sensitivity setting (enabled or disabled) for the DLP engine. By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines.
3. Disable the sensitivity setting for all DLP engines.
4. Sort the column data.
5. Disable the DLP engine.
6. Enable or disable the sensitivity setting for a specific DLP engine
7. [Show or hide the columns in the table](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
8. Search for a specific DLP engine.

[Image: The data sensitivity settings page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About External Integrations

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-external-integrations
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > About External Integrations
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about integrating AI Security with external cloud storage services.

Security information and event management (SIEM) is a solution to detect and address security threats and vulnerabilities. Data from security systems, network devices, servers, domain controllers, etc., is aggregated and analyzed to identify threats or anomalies, enabling security teams to investigate and address these issues.

You can integrate AI Security with the following external tools:

- Cloud storage services: [Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-s3), [Azure Blob Storage](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-azure-blob-storage), and [Amazon Security Lake](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-security-lake)

External integration includes the following benefits and enables you to:

- Have increased visibility into the security posture of your data.
- Reduce the number of false positive alerts and focus on real threats.
- Audit security incidents and take immediate action to remediate issues.

## About the External Integrations Page

On the Integrations page (Administration > External Integrations), you can view the following integrations:

- Cloud Storage

[Image: The Integrations page]

1. [Add a cloud storage integration](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-ai-security-cloud-storage-services).
2. View the list of cloud storage integrations. For each integration, you can see:
  - **Cloud Storage**: The name of the cloud storage service (Amazon S3 Bucket or Azure Blob Storage).
  - **Integration Name**: The integration name.
  - **Log Type**: The type of data log that is sent to the storage service.
  - **Last Sent**: The date and time when the data was last sent to the storage service.
  - **Status**: The outcome (**Success**, **Failed**, **Paused**, or **Pending**) of the previous data transfer. For failed status, hover over the label to see the reason for failure.
  - **Data Transfer**: The state (**Enabled**or **Disabled**) of data transfer. By default, the data transfer is enabled. If you want to pause the transfer without deleting the integration, click the toggle to disable the data transfer. If any data transfer is in progress, the activity is completed and then the data transfer is disabled.
3. Sort the column data.
4. Enable or disable the data transfer.
5. [Edit or delete a cloud storage integration.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-external-integrations)

[Image: View the cloud storage integrations describing the page details.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Investigation

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-investigation
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > Investigation > About Investigation
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the investigation feature in AI Security.

Your cloud resources containing data might be located in different regions. Depending on the number of cloud accounts you have onboarded, AI Security offers insights by identifying sensitive data, vulnerabilities, or any other risks in your resources.

You might want to obtain certain information related to the security posture of your cloud resources without having to create alerts or filter information on the dashboard. For example, you want to look at all S3 buckets that were scanned in the past week and check what type of sensitive data is stored in these S3 buckets. You can leverage AI Security's Investigation feature to effectively parse such information, and based on the result, save the investigation or create a custom security policy.

The Investigation feature provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Run queries on cloud resources and gain more insight into the security posture of your data.
- Customize queries, run them multiple times, inspect results, and then discard or save the queries, either as investigation queries or custom security policies.

## About the Investigation Page

On the Investigation page (AI Infrastructure > Investigation), you can do the following:

1. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) to view specific information.
2. [Add a new investigation](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/creating-new-investigation).
3. View the investigation queries that you've created. For each investigation, you can see:
  - **Cloud**: The name of the cloud service provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
  - **Query**: The query string.
  - **Resource Type**: The type of resource on which the query is run.
4. View the list of saved investigation queries.
5. Search for a query in the searchable columns.
6. [Show or hide columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
7. Click the **Actions** icon to run, save, or [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-investigation) a query. When you run a query, the investigation results are displayed. See image. Click the resource name to view the resource details.

[Image: Create a new investigation and view the previously created queries]

[Image: Investigation query results for an EC2 instance]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Issues View

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > Issues > About Issues View
- Last modified: 2026-06-04T08:20Z
- Summary: Information about AI Security issues including viewing and filtering, notifications, and model scan findings.

AI Security continuously scans your cloud resources against the [policies](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies) enabled in your cloud accounts to identify vulnerabilities and generate issues. When a policy violation is detected, AI Security generates issues and sends notifications to recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.

An issue is the outcome of a policy evaluation done on a resource type (e.g., S3 bucket, database). For example, if a security policy is enabled to detect any publicly exposed S3 bucket containing sensitive data, and there are 5 such S3 buckets in your cloud storage, AI Security generates 5 issues.

Issues are categorized by severity level to help you prioritize them and take action in a timely manner.

Issues provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- View and manage issue notifications for any security policy violations detected in the cloud accounts.
- Notify recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.
- Stay informed about critical security events.

## About the Issues Page

On the Issues View page (AI Infrastructure > Issues > Issues View), you can see the following generated issues:

1. [Apply filters to view specific data.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) By default, issues with an open status are displayed.
2. [Add additional filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
3. Search for specific data in the searchable column.
4. [Modify the table and its columns.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
5. View the list of issues generated for policy violations. For each issue, you can view:
  - **Issue ID**: The unique identifier for the issue. Clickto [view additional details](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-issue-details).
  - **Resource Name**: The name of the resource.
  - **Policy Name**: The policy title.
  - **Policy Category**: The threat category (**Public Exposure**, **Data Loss**, etc.) to which the policy belongs.
  - **Resource Type**: The type of data store (**AWS EC2 instance**, **AWS S3 bucket**, etc.).
  - **Resource ID**: The unique identifier for the resource.
  - **Risk Level**: The risk level (**Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**) of the issue. The risk level of an issue is calculated as the average of the policy severity and the resource impact. For example, if the policy severity is Critical and the resource impact is Medium, then the issue risk level is High.
  - **Issue Status**: The status (**Open**, **Closed**, **Resolved,**and**Snoozed**) of the issue.
  - **Cloud Account**: The unique identifier of the cloud account (**AWS**, **Azure**, **GCP**, **Snowflake**, and **On-Premises**) in which the resource is located.
  - **Created At**: The date and time the issue was generated.
  - **Updated At**: The date and time the issue was last updated.
6. Select one or multiple issues to [resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-issues) them.
7. Actions provide the option to **Resolve** or **Snooze** the issue. To learn more, see [Resolve an issue](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-issues) and [Snooze an issue](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-issues).

[Image: The all alerts tab displaying the list of all alerts generated by DSPM.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-embedded-ai","lastmod":"2026-07-10T10:17Z","nid":"1541556"} -->
## About Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-embedded-ai
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > About Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI
- Last modified: 2026-07-10T10:17Z
- Summary: Information about the Public AI Inventory Embedded AI apps and its features in the AI Security Admin Portal.

As organizations rapidly adopt AI capabilities embedded within everyday SaaS applications, maintaining visibility into enterprise AI usage has become increasingly challenging. Zscaler AI Security expands the AI Asset Management platform to automatically discover and identify Embedded AI applications accessed across your organization.

Unlike standalone generative AI tools, Embedded AI apps are AI-powered features built directly into popular SaaS applications, ones that employees may interact with, without explicitly recognizing them as AI. From the Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Page, security and IT teams can now understand where embedded AI is being used alongside traditional GenAI applications.

The Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Gain a complete view of your organization's AI footprint, including AI capabilities embedded within everyday SaaS applications.
- Enforce policies across both standalone Gen AI and embedded AI applications from a single platform.
- Identify applications with high risk scores or sensitive data violations before they become compliance issues.
- Detect emerging AI adoption patterns across departments and user groups to stay ahead of shadow AI usage.
- Equip security and IT teams with the context needed to make data-driven decisions about AI usage across the enterprise.

## About the Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Page

On the Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI page (Public AI > App Inventory > Embedded AI), you can do the following:

1. Filter the report for the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. **Total Apps**: View the total number of Embedded AI applications that are in use in the organization.
3. **Total Volume**: View the total bytes consumed by all the applications, both upload and download.,
4. Search for an Embedded AI app by name.
5. Show or hide columns.
6. View a list of all the Embedded AI applications. For each application, you can view:
  - **Name**: Name of the Embedded AI App. Click the app name to view additional details.
  - **Risk Index**: The risk index number.
  - **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application for both embedded and non-embedded AI traffic.
7. [Go to the Gen AI page](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-gen-ai).
8. [Go to the Endpoint AI page](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-endpoint-ai).

[Image: Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Apps page displays all the discovered embedded AI apps in your organization,]

- **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application for both embedded AI and non-embedded AI traffic.
- **Total Users**: The total number of users.
- **General Information**: Information such as policies applied, Zscaler Supported Services, Tags, Notes, Headquarters, Employees, year incorporated, activities supported, integrations, description, etc.
- **Risk Index**: The number of applications in each risk index category.
- The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
  - Risk Attributes
  - Users
  - Locations

Use this tab to view the risk attributes pertaining to the Embedded AI app. The risk attributes constitute the following:

- **Hosting Information**: Details about where the AI application is hosted, including cloud provider, region, and infrastructure information. These are risk and security posture attributes used to evaluate an app or service in an inventory, including the vendor’s compliance certifications, data retention type and description, terms of service quality, MFA support, file-sharing capabilities, data residency countries and any third-party data residency vendors, history of data breaches in the last three years, availability of admin audit logs, support for deletion upon request, source IP restriction controls, and password strength requirements.
- **Security Information**: Security features and configurations of the AI application, including authentication, data encryption, and compliance measures. These are security posture and exposure checks used to assess the risk of a domain or cloud app, covering TLS/SSL configuration (valid SSL certificate, certificate key size, signature algorithm strength, weak cipher support, SSL pinning, DNS CAA policy, encryption in transit), HTTP hardening (support for HTTP security headers), known vulnerability exposure (published CVEs and susceptibility to Logjam, Heartbleed, and POODLE), vendor security practices (vulnerability disclosure policy and support for a WAF), email authentication controls (domain-based message authentication such as SPF and DKIM), and additional risk indicators like malware content scanning, evasive behavior, and features such as remote access/screen sharing that can increase data-exposure risk.

Use this tab to view the details pertaining to the user who accessed the Embedded AI app as follows:

- Search for a specific user.
- Apply filters to view specific data.
- View a list of users that were discovered. For each user you can view:
  - **User Name:**The name of the user associated with the AI asset app activity or record
  - **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
  - **Upload Volume**: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
  - **Download Volume:**The total bytes downloaded by the application.
  - **Department:** The name of the department the user belongs to.
  - **No. of Transactions:** The total number of transactions by the user.
  - **Last Accessed:**The timestamp of when the application was last accessed.

Use this tab to view the details pertaining to the location from where the Embedded AI app was accessed as follows:

- Search for a specific location.
- Apply filters to view specific data.
- View a list of locations that were discovered. For each location you can view:
  - **Location Name**: The name of the location.
  - **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
  - **Upload Volume**: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
  - **Download Volume:**The total bytes downloaded by the application.
  - **Department:** The name of the department the user belongs to.
  - **No. of Transactions:** The total number of transactions by location.
  - **Last Accessed**: The timestamp of when the app was last accessed at the location.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

The Public AI Inventory for Endpoint AI apps helps you manage AI risk by giving you a structured, continuously updated view of the AI applications installed or used on endpoints.

The Public AI Inventory Endpoint AI Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Identify which endpoint AI apps are present and being used across devices and users.
- Group apps by category and focus first on higher-risk types, e.g., chat, remote-assist, file-sharing–heavy apps.
- Monitor whether controls reduce risky app adoption and overall exposure.

7. View a list of all the Endpoint AI applications. For each application, you can view:

  - **Total Instances:** The total number of application instances discovered.
  - **Versions:** The number of application versions available.

- **Instances:** The number of detected application instances.
- **Versions:**The number of available application versions**.**

  - Company
  - Product Name
  - Operating Platform
  - Original Filename
  - Application Type
  - Executable Filename

## About Public AI Inventory - Gen AI

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-gen-ai
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > About Public AI Inventory - Gen AI
- Last modified: 2026-06-08T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the Public AI Inventory Gen AI apps and its features in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The Public AI Inventory page in Zscaler AI Security is an up-to-date catalog of publicly accessible AI applications, such as consumer chatbots, hosted LLM APIs, and Gen AI SaaS features used across an organization. AI Security considers this inventory foundational for safe governance, as it provides visibility into sanctioned and unsanctioned (shadow) AI usage who is accessing which apps and how often.

The Public AI Inventory - Gen AI page provides centralized visibility into discovered Gen AI apps across your organization, helping you assess risk, understand adoption, and identify potential sensitive data exposure.

The Public AI Inventory - Gen AI Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Identify which Gen AI apps are being used, by whom, and across which departments.
- Reduce data risk by highlighting sensitive data sharing and upload activity to help prevent data exposure.
- Surfaces app risk signals, e.g., risk index to prioritize review and policy actions.
- Support adoption tracking by showing usage trends and top apps and users to monitor Gen AI adoption over time.

## About the Public AI Inventory - Gen AI Page

On the Public AI Inventory - Gen AI page (Public AI > App Inventory > Gen AI), you can do the following:

1. Filter the report for the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your Gen AI inventory:
  - **Total Apps**: View the total number of Gen AI applications that are in use in the organization.
  - **Total Volume**: View the total bytes consumed by all the applications, both upload and download.,
  - **Upload Volume:**View the total bytes uploaded by the application.
  - **Download Volume:** View the total bytes downloaded by the application.
  - **By Risk Index**: View the distribution of applications across each risk index category. The risk index rating is as follows:
    - Very Low–1
    - Low–2
    - Medium–3
    - High–4
    - Very High–5
3. Search for a Gen AI app by name.
4. Filter by **Risk Index**.
5. View a list of all the Gen AI applications. For each application, you can view:
  - **Name**: Name of the Gen AI App. Click the app name to view additional details.
  - **Risk Index**: The risk index number.
  - **Users**: The number of unique authenticated users who accessed the application within the specified time range.
  - **Locations**: The number of unauthenticated locations from where the application is accessed.
  - **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
  - **Upload Volume**: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
  - **Download Volume**: The total bytes downloaded by the application.

- **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application.
- **Total Users**: The total number of users.
- **General Information**: Information such as policies applied, Supported Services, Tags, Notes, Headquarters, Employees, year incorporated, activitieis supported, integrations, description.
- **Risk Index**: The number of applications in each risk index category.
- The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
  - Risk Attributes
  - Users
  - Locations

Use this tab to view the risk attributes pertaining to the Gen AI app. The risk attributes constitute the following:

- **Hosting Information**: Details about where the AI application is hosted, including cloud provider, region, and infrastructure information. These are risk and security posture attributes used to evaluate an app or service in an inventory, including the vendor’s compliance certifications, data retention type and description, terms of service quality, MFA support, file-sharing capabilities, data residency countries and any third-party data residency vendors, history of data breaches in the last three years, availability of admin audit logs, support for deletion upon request, source IP restriction controls, and password strength requirements.
- **Security Information**: Security features and configurations of the AI application, including authentication, data encryption, and compliance measures. These are security posture and exposure checks used to assess the risk of a domain or cloud app, covering TLS/SSL configuration (valid SSL certificate, certificate key size, signature algorithm strength, weak cipher support, SSL pinning, DNS CAA policy, encryption in transit), HTTP hardening (support for HTTP security headers), known vulnerability exposure (published CVEs and susceptibility to Logjam, Heartbleed, and POODLE), vendor security practices (vulnerability disclosure policy and support for a WAF), email authentication controls (domain-based message authentication such as SPF and DKIM), and additional risk indicators like malware content scanning, evasive behavior, and features such as remote access/screen sharing that can increase data-exposure risk.

Use this tab to view the details pertaining to the user who accessed the Gen AI app as follows:

- Search for a specific user.
- Apply filters to view specific data.
- View a list of users that were discovered. For each user you can view:
  - **User Name:**The name of the user associated with the AI asset app activity or record
  - **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
  - **Upload Volume**: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
  - **Download Volume:**The total bytes downloaded by the application.
  - **Department:** The name of the department the user belongs to.
  - **No. of Transactions:** The total number of transactions by the user.
  - **Last Accessed:**The timestamp of when the application was last accessed.

Use this tab to view the details pertaining to the location from where the Gen AI app was accessed as follows:

- Search for a specific location.
- Apply filters to view specific data.
- View a list of locations that were discovered. For each location you can view:
  - **Location Name**: The name of the location.
  - **Total Volume**: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
  - **Upload Volume**: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
  - **Download Volume:**The total bytes downloaded by the application.
  - **Department:** The name of the department the user belongs to.
  - **No. of Transactions:** The total number of transactions by location.
  - **Last Accessed**: The timestamp of when the app was last accessed at the location.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Public AI Overview

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-overview
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Asset Discovery > About Public AI Overview
- Last modified: 2026-07-08T08:39Z
- Summary: Information about the Public AI Overview and its features in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The Public AI Overview page in AI Security summarizes usage across Gen AI apps and Endpoint AI apps, helping you understand adoption and potential exposure. It includes an app-centric by Apps view, app usage trends over time, and breakdowns by department, top users, and locations to quickly identify where AI usage is concentrated and where activity looks unusual.

The Public AI Overview Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Quickly see which public AI apps or models are being accessed across the organization.
- Understand usage patterns, traffic, and activity volume, to spot rapid adoption or unusual spikes.
- Identify the highest-risk public AI services and usage, so teams can focus on what matters first.
- Accelerate decisions on what to allow, restrict, or block, and align usage with policy.
- Drill down from the overview into service and user details to support security reviews and incident response.

## About the Public AI - Overview Page

On the Public AI-Overview page (Public AI > Overview), you can do the following:

1. Filter the report for the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your public AI apps:
  - **Total Volume**: View the total volume of Gen AI apps used in the organization.
  - **Total Users**: View the total number of users of Gen AI apps in your organization. Click **Details**to view further details on the [**Usage Insights**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-usage-insights)page.
  - **Upload Volume:** View the total volume of data uploaded to Gen AI apps.
  - **Download Volume:** View the total volume of data downloaded from Gen AI apps.
  - **Files Uploaded**: View the total number of files uploaded to the AI apps.
3. **Gen AI Apps**: The total number of Gen AI apps used in the organization. Click **See All** to view further details on the[**Public AI Inventory - Gen AI**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-gen-ai) page.
4. **Embedded AI Apps:** The total number of embedded AI applications detected across your environment.
5. **Endpoint AI Apps**: View the number of Endpoint AI Apps used across the organization. Click **Details** to view further details onthe [**Public AI Inventory - Endpoint AI**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-desktop-apps) page.
6. **By Apps**: View the top 5 Gen AI apps used in the organization with policy actions (**Allowed**, **Blocked**, or **Isolated**) distribution for each of the apps in the form of a bar chart. Hover over the bars to view the number of transactions generated by the users. You can filter data for the Gen AI or Embedded apps and by **Total Bytes**, **Transactions**, or **Users**. Click the **Details** to view further details onthe [**Public AI Inventory - Gen AI**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-public-ai-inventory-gen-ai) page.
7. **App Usage Trends**: View the usage trends of the top 5 Gen AI apps in the form of a line chart. Hover over a date to view the AI Apps usage trend for that date. You can filter data by Gen AI or Embedded AI Apps. You can also filter the data by **Transactions**, **Users**, or **Volume**.
8. **AI Usage by Department**: View the AI Apps usage drilled down to organization departments or groups in the form of a stacked bar chart. Hover over the chart to view the Gen AI Apps usage by department. You can filter data by Gen AI or Embedded AI Apps. Click **View Details**to view further details on the [**Usage Insights**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-usage-insights)page.
9. **Top Users**: View the top users and the corresponding AI Apps used. Hover over the line severity bars to view the data distribution across the Gen AI Apps for all the users. You can filter data by Gen AI or Embedded AI Apps. You can also filter the data by **Transactions**, **Users**, or **Volume**. Click **Details** to view further details on the [**Usage Insights**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-usage-insights)page.
10. **AI Usage by Locations**: View the AI apps usage by location in the form of a bar chart. You can filter data by Gen AI or Embedded AI Apps. You can filter the data by total **Transactions**or **Total Bytes**. Click **View Details** to view further details on the [**Usage Insights**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-usage-insights)page.

## About Scan Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > About Scan Settings
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about configuring the scan settings in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Security regularly scans the cloud resources (data stores) such as cloud storage devices, databases, virtual machines. etc., within your cloud accounts and detects sensitive data and vulnerabilities. AI Security performs the scan by leveraging the [local scan orchestrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-orchestrator) that is deployed in your AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or On-Premises Data Centers account during the [onboarding process](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts). The resources are scanned against a set of standard [security policies](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies) and a scan schedule. In the scan rules, you can select the resources you want to scan, the scan type, and set the scan frequency.

The scan rule provides granular control over scan configurations. You can define custom scan types and schedules for individual data stores based on:

- Account
- Region
- Tags
- Specific resources

When scanning relational databases such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, and MySQL, AI Security uses the data sampling technique to scan a subset of data, instead of scanning the entire database. This helps to avoid a full data scan and ensures the database operations are not impacted.

You can create multiple scan rules for supported data stores such as virtual machines, databases, and Snowflake accounts.

- You need to first onboard your cloud accounts before configuring the scan rule. To learn more, see [About Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts).
- Although overlapping scan rules are allowed, they can lead to duplicate scans and increased compute costs. AI Security displays warnings during rule creation to help you avoid redundant configurations.
- If a resource is deleted from the account after configuring the scan schedule, then AI Security ignores this resource during the scan.

The scan framework in AI Security provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Use predefined DLP engines to classify sensitive data based on the level of sensitivity and risk.
- Configure the scan rule to scan your accounts and identify sensitive data.
- Regularly monitor your cloud accounts for any vulnerabilities.
- Select the required accounts for scanning and exclude some accounts from scanning.
- Configure the scan frequency and scan type.
- Use data sampling to scan a subset of data.

## Scan Types

AI Security supports the scanning of the following data stores. The scan type varies for each data store.

| Data Store | Scan Type |
| --- | --- |
| Compute | **On-Demand Scan**: Perform an on-demand scan instantly. |
| Storage | **Full Scan**: Scan all the data in the selected data or object stores. This includes both the historic data and the newer data. Newer data scan is prioritized over historic data scan.; **Scan Only New or Modified Files**: Scan only new or modified data or files in the accounts.; **Historical Scan**: Scan data or files over a lookback period in terms of days (max of 365 days). |
| Managed Database | **Full Scan**: Scan all the data in the selected data or object stores. This includes both the historic data and the newer data. Newer data scan is prioritized over historic data scan.; **Data Sampling Scan**: Scan a subset of data. |
| NoSQL Datastore | **Full Scan**: Scan all the data in the selected data or object stores. This includes both the historic data and the newer data. Newer data scan is prioritized over historic data scan.; **Scan Only Recent Data**: Scan only those files that are newly added or modified since the previous scan. This scan type is also applicable for unmanaged databases. |
| Unmanaged Database | **Data Sampling Scan**: Scan a subset of data. |

## About the Scan Settings Page

On the Scan Settings page (Administration > Scan Settings), you can see the following tabs:

- Scan Rules
- Scan Scopes

On the Scan Scopes tab, you can do the following:

1. [Create a new scan scope.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope)
2. View the scan scope configurations. For each configuration, you can view the following information:
  - **Scope**: Name of the scan scope. Click the scan scope name to view the following details.
    - Scan Scope Details
  - **Description**: A concise summary of the purpose and objectives of each scan scope.
  - **Scan Rules**: Information on whether the scan scope is linked to any specific scan rule.
  - **Created by**: The user who created the scan scope.
  - **Created on**: The date and time when the scan scope was created
3. [Show or hide the columns on the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
4. Click the **Action** icon to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-scopes) or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-scopes) the scan scope.

[Image: The Scan Scope page details all scan scopes.]

For each scan scope configuration, you can view:

1. Name of the scan scope.
2. **General Information**: Provides an overview of the scan scope, including:
  - **Created by**: Name of the user who created the scan scope.
  - **Created on**: Date and time the scan scope was created.
  - **Description**: Brief summary of the scope.
3. **Scope Criteria**: Defines the scan scope.
  - **DLP Engines**: List of the DLP engines included in the scan scope.
  - **File Type**: List of the file types included in the scan scope.
  - **ML Categories**: Whether machine learning categories are enabled or disabled for the scan scope.
4. **Scan Rules**: List of scan rules associated with the scan scope.

See image.

[Image: Scan Scope Details]

On the Scan Rule tab, you can do the following:

1. Add new scan rule for AWS, GCP, Azure, On-Premises, or Snowflake data center accounts.
2. View the scan rule configurations for various resources. For each rule configuration, you can view:
  - **Scan Rule**: Name of the scan rule. Click the scan rule name to view the following details.
    - Scan Rule Details
  - **Description**: Optional summary that explains the purpose of the scan rule.
  - **Cloud**: The name of the cloud service (AWS, Azure, GCP, or On-Premises Data Centers).
  - **Resource Type**: The type of resource or data store (cloud storage, database, or virtual machine).
  - **Scan Scope**: Information on whether the scan rule is linked to any specific scan scope.
  - **Scan Status**: The scan status indicates the state of the scanning process. To learn more, see [Understanding Scan Status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-scan-status).
  - **Scan Enable/Disable**: The enabled or disabled state of the scan setting. By default, the scan setting is disabled. After configuring the scan setting, you must [enable the scan setting](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/enabling-or-disabling-scan-rule) to initiate the scan.
  - **Added By**: Name of the user who created the scan scope.
  - **Added On**: Date and time the scan scope was created.
3. Sort the column data.
4. [Show or hide the columns in the table](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. Click the **Action** icon to:
  - [Edit or delete the scan rule](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-rule).
  - [Stop the scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/enabling-or-disabling-scan-rule).
  - [Run an on-demand scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/running-demand-scan). You can perform an on-demand scan only on databases and virtual machines.

[Image: The Scan Rules page details all scan rules.]

For each scan rule configuration, you can view:

- **Name**: Name of the scan rule.
- **Description**: Optional summary that explains the purpose of the scan rule.
- **Status**: The scan status indicates whether the scan is enabled or disabled.
- **Cloud**: The name of the cloud service (AWS, Azure, GCP, or On-Premises Data Centers).
- **Resource Type**: The type of resource or data store (cloud storage, database, or virtual machine).
- **Scan Scope**: Information on whether the scan rule is linked to any specific scan scope.
- **Scan Type**: The method used to scan the resource.
- **Resources Scanned**: The number of resources discovered and scanned by this scan rule.
- **Added On**: Date and time the scan scope was created.
- **Added By**: Name of the user who created the scan scope.

See image.

[Image: The Scan Settings page details all the scan scopes and rules.]

[Image: View the scan setting details]

## About Scanning AI Models

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Model Scan Management > About Scanning AI Models
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on AI Model Security Scanning in AI Security.

The use of large language models (LLMs) and other machine learning (ML) models has created new security blind spots. Organizations often download models from public repositories without a reliable way to inspect them for any vulnerabilities. The AI models can contain malicious code, backdoors, or embedded secrets that execute with the host application's privileges, posing a serious risk to data and systems.

AI Security AI model security provides a framework to enforce security on AI models. The AI model scanner is a command-line tool that developers and MLOps engineers can run before deploying AI models to production. You can integrate the scanner into local workflows or CI/CD pipelines to stop threats before they reach sensitive environments and ensure security across all AI model deployments.

The AI model scanner provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- **Threat Detection**: Identify malicious code, backdoors, and vulnerabilities in AI models using YARA rules and the Zscaler ThreatLabz AV engine. This prevents compromised models from entering production.
- **Secret Scanning**: Detect embedded credentials, API keys, and sensitive information across all supported file types to reduce the risk of data breaches and system compromise.
- **Code Extraction**: Extract and analyze embedded code from pickle files and Lambda layers to detect hidden malicious logic.
- **Centralized Visibility and Reporting**: Integrate scan results into the AI Security Admin Portal, providing clear reports with severity levels and remediation steps for centralized scan management, auditing, and governance.
- **Automated Security Integration**: Enable consistent, automated security checks that can be integrated into the devops pipelines.
- Prevent compromised AI models from entering production environments.
- Reduce risk of data breaches and disruption by malicious AI models.
- Enable consistent, automated security checks across development and deployment pipelines.
- Support auditing and governance through centralized reporting.

## About the Model Scan Management Page

On the Model Scan Management Page (Administration > Model Scan Management Page), you can see the following tabs:

- Integration Registration
- Download Model Scanner

[Image: Model Scan Management page showing the Integration Registration and Scanner Download tabs.]

On the **Integration Registration** tab, you can do the following:

1. [Add an integration](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations).
2. Search for specific integrations in the searchable columns.
3. View the list of model scan integrations. For each integration, you can view:
  - **Integration Name**: The name of the integration.
  - **Integration ID**: The unique identifier for the integration.
  - **Modified By**: The user who last modified the integration.
  - **Configured On**: The date and time the integration was last configured.
  - **Status**: The current status of the integration (**Enabled** or **Disabled**).
4. Sort the column data.
5. Modify the table and its columns.
6. Click the **Actions** icon to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations) or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations) an integration.

[Image: The Integration Registration tab, displaying a list of model scan integrations with their names, IDs, and statuses.]

On the **Download Model Scanner** tab, you can view the list of available AI model scanner binaries. For each scanner binary, you can view:

- **Scanner Name**: The name of the scanner binary. Click on the name to download the scanner file to your local system.
- **Scanner Version**: The version number of the scanner.
- **Operating System**: The operating system the scanner is built for (e.g., Linux, macOS).
- **Architecture**: The processor architecture (e.g., x64, Arm64).
- **Release Date**: The date the scanner binary was released.

[Image: The Scanner Download tab, showing the list of available AI Model Scanner binaries available for different operating systems.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
